# Phase 8 Prototype Baseline — What the Research Prototype Established

The facts, method and numbers from the research prototype that seeded Phase 8, restated in
this repo's terms. This is the **reproduction target** for M1–M3 (`decisions.md` O6) and the
reference for MEPS and Synthea details. Where it describes the prototype's behaviour, it
describes what was built, not what to build: the contract is [`prd.md`](./prd.md) and
[`design.md`](./design.md), and known prototype defects are listed in `design.md` §11.

**Provenance.** The prototype was built in an earlier research session and handed over on
2026-10-17 as a draft PRD, a preliminary design and developer notes with source code. Those
raw documents are **not kept in this repo** (`decisions.md` O5): their content that matters is
here, in `prd.md` (requirements, with the original `FR-*` IDs) and in `design.md`. The repo
owner holds the originals.

---

## 1. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Label `label_hosp_12m` | 1 if the person had at least one inpatient discharge in calendar year 2 of their MEPS panel (`IPDISY2 > 0`), else 0 |
| Features | Calendar-year-1 information only |
| Year 1, year 2 | The two calendar years of a MEPS two-year longitudinal panel (Panel 27 = 2022, 2023) |
| AUROC | Probability a random hospitalized person ranks above a random non-hospitalized one; 0.5 is chance |
| AUPRC | Average precision; chance equals the event rate (~0.088) |
| Brier score | Mean squared error of predicted probabilities; lower is better |
| Top-k% PPV / sensitivity | Share hospitalized among the k% highest-risk; share of all events captured there |
| Calibration | Predicted vs observed rate, by risk decile |
| Comparison model | Logistic regression on age and any year-1 inpatient stay; shown beside the main score |

## 2. Data source choices

**Training and testing: MEPS** (AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey), two-year
longitudinal panels 21–27 (2016–2023). The only real, de-identified, free, US, person-level
data found with a true 12-month prospective outcome. ICD-10-era panels only.

**MEPS use terms are ambiguous for commercial use.** The data use wording says data "may not
be used for any purpose other than for the purpose for which they were supplied". Written
confirmation from AHRQ is outstanding (`decisions.md` O23). The intended business model sells
the platform (pipeline, calibration, retraining on customer data) rather than MEPS-trained
weights alone, which reduces dependence on the answer.

**Rejected:**

| Source | Why |
|---|---|
| CPRD (UK) | ~£20,600–£83,850 per year; public-health research use only |
| OpenSAFELY (UK) | UK-based users only; aggregate outputs only |
| UK data generally | US and UK coding and care patterns differ |
| MIMIC-IV and other credentialed sets | Approved access, restricted use; MIMIC's agreement bans sending data to online services such as LLM APIs |
| Health and Retirement Study | Research and statistical purposes only |
| MCBS public file | No utilization data, so no hospitalization label |

**Synthea** — pipeline and service testing only, never accuracy (outcomes are rule-simulated).
Software Apache 2.0; published synthetic data public domain.

**Code systems:** CPT not used (AMA licence). ICD-10-CM free in the US. SNOMED CT and the NLM
SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM map free in the US with a UMLS licence.

**Regulatory posture:** a non-time-critical risk score shown to clinicians with its basis
visible — likely outside FDA device rules or under enforcement discretion per the FDA clinical
decision support guidance. Needs counsel's review before launch.

**Benchmark:** QAdmissions (UK) reports AUROC 0.77–0.78 and top-decile PPV of 42% for
*emergency* admission — a different outcome, so compare with care.

## 3. MEPS facts

### 3.1 Files

Stata files: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip` (contains `h{n}.dta`).
Documentation: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h{n}/h{n}doc.shtml`.
The folder-less form (`…/pufs/h252dta.zip`) returns 404. Extract with Python `zipfile`; don't
assume an `unzip` binary. First download is ~40 MB.

| Panel | Years | File | Persons in file | Adults kept | Events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 2016–2017 | HC-202 | 15,617 | 11,174 | 880 |
| 22 | 2017–2018 | HC-210 | 14,541 | 10,613 | 940 |
| 23 | 2018–2019 | HC-217 | 14,067 | 10,447 | 989 |
| 24 | 2019–2020 | HC-225 | 9,797 | 7,533 | 592 |
| 25 | 2020–2021 | HC-234 | 6,078 | 4,730 | 377 |
| 26 | 2021–2022 | HC-244 | 6,741 | 5,350 | 453 |
| 27 | 2022–2023 | HC-252 | 8,292 | 6,513 | 589 |
| **Total** | | | | **56,360** | **4,820 (8.6%)** |

**Exclude HC-245**: a Panel 24 three-year file (5,565 persons). It has `IPDISY2` and looks
like a longitudinal file, but duplicates Panel 24 people.

2022 event files examined (also `h{n}dta.zip`):

| File | Content | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| HC-241 | Medical Conditions | 83,173 | 33 |
| HC-239A | Prescribed Medicines | 232,605 | 65 |
| HC-239D | Hospital Inpatient Stays | 1,933 | 50 |
| HC-239G | Office-Based Visits | 151,263 | 46 |
| HC-239I | Condition-event link | not downloaded | |
| HC-239B/C/E/F/H | Dental, other medical, ER, outpatient, home health | not downloaded | |

For other years, look file numbers up on the MEPS data files page and verify each by
downloading and checking `PANEL` or the year in variable labels. Never guess a file number.

### 3.2 Variable naming

- `Y1` / `Y2` suffix: panel year 1 / year 2 (`IPDISY1`, `IPDISY2`).
- Trailing digit 1–5: interview round (`RTHLTH1`, `ADBMI2`, `OFTSMK3`).
- `X` suffix: edited or imputed. `_M18`: question modified in 2018 (`DIABDXY1_M18`).
- **Round 3 ends in year 2 for almost everyone** — in HC-252, 6,518 of 6,546 adults, mostly
  January–April. Treat round-3 items as possible leakage.
- Self-administered questionnaire items are round 2, ~63–67% valid among adults (`ADBMI2`,
  `K6SUM2`, `VPCS2`). Diabetes-care items (`DS*`, round 3) are sparse — e.g. 350 adults for
  `DSA1C3` in HC-252.

### 3.3 Coding

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Yes/no | 1 = yes, 2 = no (not 0/1) — recode |
| Exceptions | `DIED`, `INST`: 0 = no, 1 = yes |
| Missing | -1 inapplicable, -2 determined in previous round, -7 refused, -8 don't know, -9 not ascertained, -15 cannot be computed |
| Strings | Missing is the string `-15` (e.g. `ICD10CDX`) |
| Income | Can be truly negative (business losses) — not missing |
| Age | Top-coded at 85 |
| Money | Person totals int32 whole dollars; event-level float64. MEPS money is **payments**, not charges |

2,622 of 2,648 HC-252 variables carry value labels, including counts and amounts, because the
labels describe the negative codes.

### 3.4 Storage types

| File | Storage counts |
|---|---|
| HC-252 | 1,603 int8, 611 int16, 383 int32, 25 float64, 26 strings (21 str2, 2 str3, 2 str9, 1 str10) |
| HC-241 | 20 int8, 4 int16, 1 float64, 8 strings |
| HC-239A | 20 int8, 20 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 11 strings |
| HC-239D | 12 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 27 float64, 4 strings |
| HC-239G | 23 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 3 strings |

Key strings: `DUPERSID` str10; `CONDIDX` str13; `EVNTIDX` str16; `RXRECIDX` str19; `LINKIDX`
str16; `DRUGIDX` str13; `ICD10CDX` declared str8, always 3 characters (281 distinct in 2022);
`CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X` str6 (e.g. `CIR007`); `RXNDC` str11 with leading zeros (8,649 distinct);
`RXNAME` str50 (1,585 distinct, abbreviated); `RXDRGNAM` str60 (max 47 used); `RXFORM`,
`RXFRMUNT`, `RXSTRENG`, `RXSTRUNT` str50 (short codes; strength is text). Multum classes `TC1`,
`TC1S1`, `TC1S1_1` are int16.

pandas' `StataReader` exposes storage types only through the private `_typlist`/`_lbllist`
attributes after `read()` — codes `b` int8, `h` int16, `l` int32, `f` float32, `d` float64, an
integer N = strN. Stable in pandas 2.x and 3.x, but private: pin and test.

### 3.5 What MEPS does not have

No free text (condition verbatims were coded by AHRQ and not released; "other, specify" is
code 91 only), no lab values, no vitals except BMI, no procedure codes, no full ICD-10 codes,
no exact dates (month and year only), no geography finer than 4 census regions, no provider
identity.

## 4. The prototype's method

### 4.1 Dataset build

- Per panel, read the `.dta` with `convert_categoricals=False` and select: `DUPERSID, PANEL,
  SEX, RACETHX, REGIONY1, AGEY1X, INSCOVY1, POVCATY1, IPDISY1, IPNGTDY1, ERTOTY1, OBTOTVY1,
  OPTOTVY1, HHTOTDY1, RXTOTY1, TOTEXPY1, IPDISY2, LONGWT, VARSTR, VARPSU`.
- Diagnosis flags from prefixes `HIBPDX, CHDDX, ANGIDX, MIDX, OHRTDX, STRKDX, EMPHDX, DIABDX,
  ARTHDX, ASTHDX, CHOLDX`: the first column (sorted) starting with the prefix and containing
  `Y1`; recoded `== 1` → 1, everything else → 0.
- Keep `AGEY1X >= 18`, `IPDISY1 >= 0`, `IPDISY2 >= 0`. Label = `IPDISY2 > 0`; drop `IPDISY2`;
  lower-case column names. Output shape `(56360, 31)`.

### 4.2 Training

- Features: every column except `dupersid, panel, label_hosp_12m, longwt, varstr, varpsu` —
  the 25 contract features in contract order (`design.md` §3).
- Categoricals `sex, racethx, regiony1, inscovy1, povcaty1`: clipped at 0 (negative MEPS codes
  → category 0), cast to int.
- `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=0,
  categorical_features=<indices of the five>)`.
- Validation model: panels 21–25; test: 26–27. Release model refit on all panels.
- Comparison model: `LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)` on `[agey1x, ipdisy1 > 0]`, panels
  21–25.

### 4.3 Evaluation

Bootstrap 95% CIs: 500 resamples of the test set, `numpy.random.default_rng(0)`. Top-k: sort
by descending score, take `int(n × k)`. Deciles: `pandas.qcut(p, 10)`. Survey-weighted AUROC:
`sample_weight=LONGWT`. Null Brier: training-panel event rate as a constant prediction.
Permutation importance: `n_repeats=5, random_state=0, scoring='roc_auc'` on the test panels.

### 4.4 Environment used

Python 3.14.3, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, numpy 2.5.4; Temurin 17 JRE for Synthea.
Python 3.11+ with pandas 2.2+ and scikit-learn 1.5+ is expected to work; small metric
differences can come from library versions. Pickled models are not portable across
scikit-learn versions — retrain, never copy a `.pkl`.

## 5. Numbers to reproduce

### 5.1 Dataset (M1) — exact

56,360 rows, 4,820 events, per-panel counts as §3.1. HC-252 dictionary: 2,648 variables, storage
counts as §3.4.

### 5.2 Model (M2) — within tolerance

`n_train 44497`, `n_test 11863`, `events_test 1042`, rate 0.0878.

| Measure | Comparison model | Gradient boosting |
|---|---|---|
| AUROC [95% CI] | 0.708 [0.691, 0.725] | 0.769 [0.754, 0.786] |
| **Tolerance** | **0.700–0.716** | **0.760–0.778** |
| AUPRC [95% CI] | 0.225 [0.206, 0.250] | 0.265 [0.242, 0.290] |
| Brier (null 0.0801) | 0.0751 | 0.0725 |
| Mean predicted | 0.0902 | 0.0917 |
| Top 5% PPV / sens | 0.331 / 0.188 | 0.383 / 0.218 |
| Top 10% PPV / sens | 0.266 / 0.303 | 0.293 / 0.333 |
| Top 20% PPV / sens | 0.202 / 0.460 | 0.231 / 0.525 |
| Survey-weighted AUROC | | 0.780 |

Calibration deciles (predicted / actual), lowest to highest: 0.016/0.008, 0.023/0.013,
0.034/0.025, 0.045/0.041, 0.056/0.056, 0.071/0.072, 0.089/0.095, 0.117/0.107, 0.162/0.169,
0.304/0.292.

| Subgroup (GBM) | n | Events | Rate | AUROC | Mean predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18–44 | 4,362 | 193 | 0.044 | 0.761 | 0.054 |
| 45–64 | 3,965 | 273 | 0.069 | 0.739 | 0.079 |

0.0057, `obtotvy1` 0.0057, `ipngtdy1` 0.0054, `totexpy1` 0.0053, `ertoty1` 0.0045, `povcaty1`
0.0045, `arthdx` 0.0024.

Comparison model coefficients (panels 21–25): intercept -4.047, age 0.0280 per year, prior stay
1.3055 — each 10 years × 1.32 odds; a prior stay × 3.7. Predicted risk without/with prior
stay: age 30 3.9%/13.0%; 50 6.6%/20.7%; 70 11.0%/31.4%; 85 15.9%/41.0%.

**Childbirth in the label** (all panels): ages 18–44, men 2.2% vs women 7.4%; 45–64, 7.4% vs
7.6%; 65+, 16.0% vs 16.0%. The motivation for M9.

## 6. Synthea harness (prototype run)

### 6.1 Generation

Seed 42, 3,000 requested (3,712 written, including deceased), ages 18–90, end date
2024-12-31, Arizona, CSV export only, `-Xmx6g`, ~10 minutes, run in the foreground with a
timeout (backgrounded runs were killed). The prototype used `master-branch-latest`; Phase 8
uses the repo's pinned v4.0.0 (O11), so its counts will differ. Synthea's public 108-patient
Massachusetts CSV sample is a usable quick fixture.

### 6.2 Format facts

- Conditions, encounter reasons, procedures: SNOMED CT. Medications: RxNorm. Observations:
  LOINC. Immunizations: CVX. No ICD-10 in the CSV export.
- Encounter classes: ambulatory, wellness, outpatient, emergency, urgentcare, home, inpatient,
  snf, hospice, virtual.
- Dates are ISO 8601 with time zone — make them time-zone-naive before comparing or pandas
  raises `Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware`.
- `patients.csv` has `INCOME` and `STATE`, no household size.
- `payers.csv` `OWNERSHIP` is GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE or NO_INSURANCE.

### 6.3 Mapping rules (prototype, training mode, year 1 = calendar year Y)

| Feature | Rule |
|---|---|
| Population | Born on or before 12/31/Y, alive on 12/31/Y, age ≥ 18 |
| `agey1x` | `int((12/31/Y − birth).days / 365.25)`, capped at 85 |
| `sex` | M → 1, F → 2 |
| `racethx` | Hispanic → 1; else white 2, black 3, asian 4, other 5 |
| `regiony1` | State → Northeast 1, Midwest 2, West 4, anything else 3 (**defect** — contract says unknown → 0) |
| `povcaty1` | `INCOME` / HHS poverty guideline (1-person household assumed: 2022 $13,590, 2023 $14,580, 2024 $15,060) × 100: <100 → 1, <125 → 2, <200 → 3, <400 → 4, else 5 |
| `inscovy1` | Any PRIVATE payer overlapping year 1 → 1; else any GOVERNMENT → 2; else 3 |
| `ipdisy1` / `ipngtdy1` | Count / summed rounded nights of inpatient encounters starting in year 1 |
| `ertoty1` | Emergency encounters |
| `obtotvy1` | Ambulatory + wellness + urgentcare + virtual |
| `optotvy1` | Outpatient |
| `hhtotdy1` | Home encounters (one per day) |
| `rxtoty1` | `DISPENSES` prorated by overlap of [START, STOP] with year 1; missing STOP → end of year 2 (**leakage defect**) |
| `totexpy1` | Year-1 `TOTAL_CLAIM_COST` + prorated medication `TOTALCOST`, whole dollars (charges, not payments) |
| Diagnosis flags | Any condition with `START` ≤ 12/31/Y whose lower-cased description matches the pattern below |
| `label_hosp_12m` | Any inpatient encounter starting in year Y+1 |

Description patterns (stand-ins until M11's code lists): `hibpdx` `hypertension`; `chddx`
`ischemic heart disease|coronary artery`; `angidx` `angina`; `midx` `myocardial infarction`;
`ohrtdx` `heart failure|atrial fibrillation|cardiomyopathy|valve|arrhythmia`; `strkdx`
`stroke|cerebrovascular accident|cerebral infarction`; `emphdx` `emphysema|chronic
obstructive`; `diabdx` `(?<!pre)diabetes`; `arthdx` `arthritis|osteoarthritis`; `asthdx`
`asthma`; `choldx` `hyperlipidemia|hypercholesterolemia|hypertriglyceridemia`.

**Regression case:** bare `coronary` matched "Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging
heart+coronary circulat (finding)". The narrowed pattern must never match it.

### 6.4 Results and lessons

- Year 1 = 2023: 2,913 adults; 138 hospitalized in 2024 (4.7%); mean predicted 10.5%; AUROC
  0.656. **A mechanical pipeline check, not an accuracy measure.**
- Even after the `coronary` fix, 25.1% of Synthea adults have coronary heart disease vs 5.6%
  in MEPS — the simulator, not the mapping.
- MEPS vs Synthea: median spending $1,728 vs $15,082 (payments vs charges); mean fills 12.6 vs
  33.8; arthritis 27% vs 12%; asthma 13% vs 4%; any home health 4.4% vs 0.4%; year-1
  hospitalization 7.9% vs 4.7%.
- Dropping spending, fills and home health: Synthea AUROC 0.651 → 0.673; MEPS AUROC
  0.766 → 0.768 (`decisions.md` O25).

## 8. Pointers for M9–M11

- **Unplanned-stay label (M9):** yearly Hospital Inpatient Stays files (HC-239D for 2022 and

  pregnancy complications, 91 other. `EMERROOM` 1 = began in ER. Dates month/year only
  (`IPBEGMM`, `IPBEGYR`). Link on `DUPERSID`.
- **Condition features (M10):** Medical Conditions `ICD10CDX` (3 characters) and
  `CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X`; ~10% of codes suppressed as `-15`; only conditions linked to an event that

- **Tuning (M10):** panel-grouped CV within 21–25; 26–27 never touched.

# Phase 8 Prototype Baseline — What the Research Prototype Established

The facts, method and numbers from the research prototype that seeded Phase 8, restated in
this repo's terms. This is the **reproduction target** for M1–M3 (`decisions.md` O6) and the
reference for MEPS and Synthea details. Where it describes the prototype's behaviour, it
describes what was built, not what to build: the contract is [`prd.md`](./prd.md) and
[`design.md`](./design.md), and known prototype defects are listed in `design.md` §11.

**Provenance.** The prototype was built in an earlier research session and handed over on
2026-10-17 as a draft PRD, a preliminary design and developer notes with source code. Those
raw documents are **not kept in this repo** (`decisions.md` O5): their content that matters is
here, in `prd.md` (requirements, with the original `FR-*` IDs) and in `design.md`. The repo
owner holds the originals.

---

## 1. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Label `label_hosp_12m` | 1 if the person had at least one inpatient discharge in calendar year 2 of their MEPS panel (`IPDISY2 > 0`), else 0 |
| Features | Calendar-year-1 information only |
| Year 1, year 2 | The two calendar years of a MEPS two-year longitudinal panel (Panel 27 = 2022, 2023) |
| AUROC | Probability a random hospitalized person ranks above a random non-hospitalized one; 0.5 is chance |
| AUPRC | Average precision; chance equals the event rate (~0.088) |
| Brier score | Mean squared error of predicted probabilities; lower is better |
| Top-k% PPV / sensitivity | Share hospitalized among the k% highest-risk; share of all events captured there |
| Calibration | Predicted vs observed rate, by risk decile |
| Comparison model | Logistic regression on age and any year-1 inpatient stay; shown beside the main score |

## 2. Data source choices

**Training and testing: MEPS** (AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey), two-year
longitudinal panels 21–27 (2016–2023). The only real, de-identified, free, US, person-level
data found with a true 12-month prospective outcome. ICD-10-era panels only.

**MEPS use terms are ambiguous for commercial use.** The data use wording says data "may not
be used for any purpose other than for the purpose for which they were supplied". Written
confirmation from AHRQ is outstanding (`decisions.md` O23). The intended business model sells
the platform (pipeline, calibration, retraining on customer data) rather than MEPS-trained
weights alone, which reduces dependence on the answer.

**Rejected:**

| Source | Why |
|---|---|
| CPRD (UK) | ~£20,600–£83,850 per year; public-health research use only |
| OpenSAFELY (UK) | UK-based users only; aggregate outputs only |
| UK data generally | US and UK coding and care patterns differ |
| MIMIC-IV and other credentialed sets | Approved access, restricted use; MIMIC's agreement bans sending data to online services such as LLM APIs |
| Health and Retirement Study | Research and statistical purposes only |
| MCBS public file | No utilization data, so no hospitalization label |

**Synthea** — pipeline and service testing only, never accuracy (outcomes are rule-simulated).
Software Apache 2.0; published synthetic data public domain.

**Code systems:** CPT not used (AMA licence). ICD-10-CM free in the US. SNOMED CT and the NLM
SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM map free in the US with a UMLS licence.

**Regulatory posture:** a non-time-critical risk score shown to clinicians with its basis
visible — likely outside FDA device rules or under enforcement discretion per the FDA clinical
decision support guidance. Needs counsel's review before launch.

**Benchmark:** QAdmissions (UK) reports AUROC 0.77–0.78 and top-decile PPV of 42% for
*emergency* admission — a different outcome, so compare with care.

## 3. MEPS facts

### 3.1 Files

Stata files: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip` (contains `h{n}.dta`).
Documentation: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h{n}/h{n}doc.shtml`.
The folder-less form (`…/pufs/h252dta.zip`) returns 404. Extract with Python `zipfile`; don't
assume an `unzip` binary. First download is ~40 MB.

| Panel | Years | File | Persons in file | Adults kept | Events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 2016–2017 | HC-202 | 15,617 | 11,174 | 880 |
| 22 | 2017–2018 | HC-210 | 14,541 | 10,613 | 940 |
| 23 | 2018–2019 | HC-217 | 14,067 | 10,447 | 989 |
| 24 | 2019–2020 | HC-225 | 9,797 | 7,533 | 592 |
| 25 | 2020–2021 | HC-234 | 6,078 | 4,730 | 377 |
| 26 | 2021–2022 | HC-244 | 6,741 | 5,350 | 453 |
| 27 | 2022–2023 | HC-252 | 8,292 | 6,513 | 589 |
| **Total** | | | | **56,360** | **4,820 (8.6%)** |

**Exclude HC-245**: a Panel 24 three-year file (5,565 persons). It has `IPDISY2` and looks
like a longitudinal file, but duplicates Panel 24 people.

2022 event files examined (also `h{n}dta.zip`):

| File | Content | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| HC-241 | Medical Conditions | 83,173 | 33 |
| HC-239A | Prescribed Medicines | 232,605 | 65 |
| HC-239D | Hospital Inpatient Stays | 1,933 | 50 |
| HC-239G | Office-Based Visits | 151,263 | 46 |
| HC-239I | Condition-event link | not downloaded | |
| HC-239B/C/E/F/H | Dental, other medical, ER, outpatient, home health | not downloaded | |

For other years, look file numbers up on the MEPS data files page and verify each by
downloading and checking `PANEL` or the year in variable labels. Never guess a file number.

### 3.2 Variable naming

- `Y1` / `Y2` suffix: panel year 1 / year 2 (`IPDISY1`, `IPDISY2`).
- Trailing digit 1–5: interview round (`RTHLTH1`, `ADBMI2`, `OFTSMK3`).
- `X` suffix: edited or imputed. `_M18`: question modified in 2018 (`DIABDXY1_M18`).
- **Round 3 ends in year 2 for almost everyone** — in HC-252, 6,518 of 6,546 adults, mostly
  January–April. Treat round-3 items as possible leakage.
- Self-administered questionnaire items are round 2, ~63–67% valid among adults (`ADBMI2`,
  `K6SUM2`, `VPCS2`). Diabetes-care items (`DS*`, round 3) are sparse — e.g. 350 adults for
  `DSA1C3` in HC-252.

### 3.3 Coding

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Yes/no | 1 = yes, 2 = no (not 0/1) — recode |
| Exceptions | `DIED`, `INST`: 0 = no, 1 = yes |
| Missing | -1 inapplicable, -2 determined in previous round, -7 refused, -8 don't know, -9 not ascertained, -15 cannot be computed |
| Strings | Missing is the string `-15` (e.g. `ICD10CDX`) |
| Income | Can be truly negative (business losses) — not missing |
| Age | Top-coded at 85 |
| Money | Person totals int32 whole dollars; event-level float64. MEPS money is **payments**, not charges |

2,622 of 2,648 HC-252 variables carry value labels, including counts and amounts, because the
labels describe the negative codes.

### 3.4 Storage types

| File | Storage counts |
|---|---|
| HC-252 | 1,603 int8, 611 int16, 383 int32, 25 float64, 26 strings (21 str2, 2 str3, 2 str9, 1 str10) |
| HC-241 | 20 int8, 4 int16, 1 float64, 8 strings |
| HC-239A | 20 int8, 20 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 11 strings |
| HC-239D | 12 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 27 float64, 4 strings |
| HC-239G | 23 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 3 strings |

Key strings: `DUPERSID` str10; `CONDIDX` str13; `EVNTIDX` str16; `RXRECIDX` str19; `LINKIDX`
str16; `DRUGIDX` str13; `ICD10CDX` declared str8, always 3 characters (281 distinct in 2022);
`CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X` str6 (e.g. `CIR007`); `RXNDC` str11 with leading zeros (8,649 distinct);
`RXNAME` str50 (1,585 distinct, abbreviated); `RXDRGNAM` str60 (max 47 used); `RXFORM`,
`RXFRMUNT`, `RXSTRENG`, `RXSTRUNT` str50 (short codes; strength is text). Multum classes `TC1`,
`TC1S1`, `TC1S1_1` are int16.

pandas' `StataReader` exposes storage types only through the private `_typlist`/`_lbllist`
attributes after `read()` — codes `b` int8, `h` int16, `l` int32, `f` float32, `d` float64, an
integer N = strN. Stable in pandas 2.x and 3.x, but private: pin and test.

### 3.5 What MEPS does not have

No free text (condition verbatims were coded by AHRQ and not released; "other, specify" is
code 91 only), no lab values, no vitals except BMI, no procedure codes, no full ICD-10 codes,
no exact dates (month and year only), no geography finer than 4 census regions, no provider
identity.

## 4. The prototype's method

### 4.1 Dataset build

- Per panel, read the `.dta` with `convert_categoricals=False` and select: `DUPERSID, PANEL,
  SEX, RACETHX, REGIONY1, AGEY1X, INSCOVY1, POVCATY1, IPDISY1, IPNGTDY1, ERTOTY1, OBTOTVY1,
  OPTOTVY1, HHTOTDY1, RXTOTY1, TOTEXPY1, IPDISY2, LONGWT, VARSTR, VARPSU`.
- Diagnosis flags from prefixes `HIBPDX, CHDDX, ANGIDX, MIDX, OHRTDX, STRKDX, EMPHDX, DIABDX,
  ARTHDX, ASTHDX, CHOLDX`: the first column (sorted) starting with the prefix and containing
  `Y1`; recoded `== 1` → 1, everything else → 0.
- Keep `AGEY1X >= 18`, `IPDISY1 >= 0`, `IPDISY2 >= 0`. Label = `IPDISY2 > 0`; drop `IPDISY2`;
  lower-case column names. Output shape `(56360, 31)`.

### 4.2 Training

- Features: every column except `dupersid, panel, label_hosp_12m, longwt, varstr, varpsu` —
  the 25 contract features in contract order (`design.md` §3).
- Categoricals `sex, racethx, regiony1, inscovy1, povcaty1`: clipped at 0 (negative MEPS codes
  → category 0), cast to int.
- `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=0,
  categorical_features=<indices of the five>)`.
- Validation model: panels 21–25; test: 26–27. Release model refit on all panels.
- Comparison model: `LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)` on `[agey1x, ipdisy1 > 0]`, panels
  21–25.

### 4.3 Evaluation

Bootstrap 95% CIs: 500 resamples of the test set, `numpy.random.default_rng(0)`. Top-k: sort
by descending score, take `int(n × k)`. Deciles: `pandas.qcut(p, 10)`. Survey-weighted AUROC:
`sample_weight=LONGWT`. Null Brier: training-panel event rate as a constant prediction.
Permutation importance: `n_repeats=5, random_state=0, scoring='roc_auc'` on the test panels.

### 4.4 Environment used

Python 3.14.3, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, numpy 2.5.4; Temurin 17 JRE for Synthea.
Python 3.11+ with pandas 2.2+ and scikit-learn 1.5+ is expected to work; small metric
differences can come from library versions. Pickled models are not portable across
scikit-learn versions — retrain, never copy a `.pkl`.

## 5. Numbers to reproduce

56,360 rows, 4,820 events, per-panel counts as §3.1. HC-252 dictionary: 2,648 variables, storage
counts as §3.4.

## 6. Synthea harness (prototype run)

### 6.1 Generation

Seed 42, 3,000 requested (3,712 written, including deceased), ages 18–90, end date
2024-12-31, Arizona, CSV export only, `-Xmx6g`, ~10 minutes, run in the foreground with a
timeout (backgrounded runs were killed). The prototype used `master-branch-latest`; Phase 8
uses the repo's pinned v4.0.0 (O11), so its counts will differ. Synthea's public 108-patient
Massachusetts CSV sample is a usable quick fixture.

### 6.2 Format facts

- Conditions, encounter reasons, procedures: SNOMED CT. Medications: RxNorm. Observations:
  LOINC. Immunizations: CVX. No ICD-10 in the CSV export.
- Encounter classes: ambulatory, wellness, outpatient, emergency, urgentcare, home, inpatient,
  snf, hospice, virtual.
- Dates are ISO 8601 with time zone — make them time-zone-naive before comparing or pandas
  raises `Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware`.
- `patients.csv` has `INCOME` and `STATE`, no household size.
- `payers.csv` `OWNERSHIP` is GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE or NO_INSURANCE.

### 6.3 Mapping rules (prototype, training mode, year 1 = calendar year Y)

| Feature | Rule |
|---|---|
| Population | Born on or before 12/31/Y, alive on 12/31/Y, age ≥ 18 |
| `agey1x` | `int((12/31/Y − birth).days / 365.25)`, capped at 85 |
| `sex` | M → 1, F → 2 |
| `racethx` | Hispanic → 1; else white 2, black 3, asian 4, other 5 |
| `regiony1` | State → Northeast 1, Midwest 2, West 4, anything else 3 (**defect** — contract says unknown → 0) |
| `povcaty1` | `INCOME` / HHS poverty guideline (1-person household assumed: 2022 $13,590, 2023 $14,580, 2024 $15,060) × 100: <100 → 1, <125 → 2, <200 → 3, <400 → 4, else 5 |
| `inscovy1` | Any PRIVATE payer overlapping year 1 → 1; else any GOVERNMENT → 2; else 3 |
| `ipdisy1` / `ipngtdy1` | Count / summed rounded nights of inpatient encounters starting in year 1 |
| `ertoty1` | Emergency encounters |
| `obtotvy1` | Ambulatory + wellness + urgentcare + virtual |
| `optotvy1` | Outpatient |
| `hhtotdy1` | Home encounters (one per day) |
| `rxtoty1` | `DISPENSES` prorated by overlap of [START, STOP] with year 1; missing STOP → end of year 2 (**leakage defect**) |
| `totexpy1` | Year-1 `TOTAL_CLAIM_COST` + prorated medication `TOTALCOST`, whole dollars (charges, not payments) |
| Diagnosis flags | Any condition with `START` ≤ 12/31/Y whose lower-cased description matches the pattern below |
| `label_hosp_12m` | Any inpatient encounter starting in year Y+1 |

Description patterns (stand-ins until M11's code lists): `hibpdx` `hypertension`; `chddx`
`ischemic heart disease|coronary artery`; `angidx` `angina`; `midx` `myocardial infarction`;
`ohrtdx` `heart failure|atrial fibrillation|cardiomyopathy|valve|arrhythmia`; `strkdx`
`stroke|cerebrovascular accident|cerebral infarction`; `emphdx` `emphysema|chronic
obstructive`; `diabdx` `(?<!pre)diabetes`; `arthdx` `arthritis|osteoarthritis`; `asthdx`
`asthma`; `choldx` `hyperlipidemia|hypercholesterolemia|hypertriglyceridemia`.

**Regression case:** bare `coronary` matched "Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging
heart+coronary circulat (finding)". The narrowed pattern must never match it.

### 6.4 Results and lessons

- Year 1 = 2023: 2,913 adults; 138 hospitalized in 2024 (4.7%); mean predicted 10.5%; AUROC
  0.656. **A mechanical pipeline check, not an accuracy measure.**
- Even after the `coronary` fix, 25.1% of Synthea adults have coronary heart disease vs 5.6%
  in MEPS — the simulator, not the mapping.
- MEPS vs Synthea: median spending $1,728 vs $15,082 (payments vs charges); mean fills 12.6 vs
  33.8; arthritis 27% vs 12%; asthma 13% vs 4%; any home health 4.4% vs 0.4%; year-1
  hospitalization 7.9% vs 4.7%.
- Dropping spending, fills and home health: Synthea AUROC 0.651 → 0.673; MEPS AUROC
  0.766 → 0.768 (`decisions.md` O25).

## 8. Pointers for M9–M11

- **Unplanned-stay label (M9):** yearly Hospital Inpatient Stays files (HC-239D for 2022 and
  equivalents), using the year-2 calendar year's file per panel. `RSNINHOS`: 1 surgery, 2
  treatment/therapy, 3 diagnostic tests only, 4 give birth (mother), 5 to be born (baby), 6
  pregnancy complications, 91 other. `EMERROOM` 1 = began in ER. Dates month/year only
  (`IPBEGMM`, `IPBEGYR`). Link on `DUPERSID`.
- **Condition features (M10):** Medical Conditions `ICD10CDX` (3 characters) and
  `CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X`; ~10% of codes suppressed as `-15`; only conditions linked to an event that
  year are present.
- **Drug features (M10):** Prescribed Medicines `RXNDC`, `TC1`, `TC1S1`, `TC1S1_1`, `RXDAYSUP`
  (999 = as needed; missing not imputed). Multum classes changed across years — check when
  pooling.
- **Event files are yearly:** for panel P with year 1 = Y, use year-Y files filtered to
  `PANEL == P`.
- **Tuning (M10):** panel-grouped CV within 21–25; 26–27 never touched.
- **Code lists (M11):** NLM SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM map (UMLS licence). For a later claims
  adapter, CMS Synthetic RIF files carry ICD-10-CM, HCPCS and NDC.
- Area-level enrichment candidates (later contract versions): AHRQ Community-Level Health
  Database; CDC PLACES.

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| AHRQ declines commercial use of MEPS-trained models | Ask in writing now (O23); sell the platform and retraining, not weights |
| Employer IP agreement claims the work | Repo owner reviews their employment agreement before building on work time or equipment |
| Survey (MEPS) vs records (customer) mismatch | Portable features first (O25); recalibrate per customer (Phase 8b); validate on customer history |
| Synthea mistaken for accuracy evidence | Every report says Synthea results are pipeline tests only |
| Weak 65+ performance | M10 |
| Childbirth and planned stays in the label | M9 |
| Regulatory change | Counsel reviews the FDA CDS position before launch |

-2. **Deterministic services decide, AI explains.** The risk score comes from a deterministic, versioned model. Any LLM use is limited to explaining results or helping development, never computing the score, and never with real patient data.
-3. **Training and scoring are separate modes.** Training mode may look at year 2 to build the label. Scoring mode must never read data after the scoring date.
-4. **Portable features first.** The core model uses features that also exist in claims or medical records. Survey-only features are an optional add-on group.
-5. **Reproducible by one command per stage.** Fixed seeds, pinned versions, cached downloads, recorded checksums.

-# Product Requirements Document: 12-Month Hospitalization Risk Service
-Version: 0.1 (research prototype complete, production build not started)
-Audience: the product owner, and Claude Code working in a fresh session. Claude Code should read this document first, then `02_Preliminary_Design.md`, then `03_Developer_Notes.md`.

-Build a production-ready cloud service that estimates each adult patient's probability of at least one inpatient hospital stay in the next 12 months. Train and test it only on free, open, US-based data that permits later commercialization. The first target customer type is a chain of US primary care clinics, especially risk-bearing practices that serve Medicare patients.

-A research prototype already exists and was built in an earlier session. It is described in section 9. The immediate job for Claude Code is to reproduce that prototype in a GitHub repository, with tests, and then extend it as described in the phases below.

-Primary care teams in value-based contracts are paid to keep patients out of the hospital. They need a ranked list of who is most likely to be hospitalized in the next year, so care managers can reach out early. Commercial risk scores exist but are proprietary and expensive, and they are often trained on data the vendor cannot share. The user wants to own a model and pipeline whose training data and code can be inspected, reproduced and commercialized.
-| Care manager or nurse | A ranked list of patients, with the reasons each one is high risk |
-| Primary care clinician | A per-patient risk score at the point of care, easy to sanity check |
-| Population health or analytics lead | Calibrated risk for budgeting and staffing; performance reports by subgroup |
-| Customer IT or data engineering team | A documented input schema and a way to send records (FHIR or claims) |
-| Product owner (the user) | A reproducible pipeline, clear licensing position, and a path to sell the platform |
-1. Predict 12-month hospitalization risk for adults (18 and older).
-2. Use only free, open, US-based data for training and testing.
-3. Keep the freedom to commercialize later.
-4. Use AI tools (Claude Code) to do the engineering work.
-5. Run as a cloud service with an API.
-6. Accept real medical records or claims from a customer, convert them into the model's input schema automatically, and score them.
-7. Show both a complex model score and a simple, hand-checkable comparison score.
-- Free-text features (doctor's notes, NLP, sentiment analysis). The training data has no free text. Revisit only when a customer's notes are available.
-- Real-time or emergency use. This is a yearly planning tool, not an alarm.
-- Training on customer data inside this repository. Customer data never enters the repo.
-- UK or other non-US data sources.
-| Outcome is any inpatient stay in the next calendar year | User's chosen focus | User instruction |
-| Data must be open, free and allow commercialization | User's chosen constraint | User instruction |

-| Primary training data is MEPS (AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey) two-year longitudinal panels 21 to 27 (2016 to 2023) | Only real, de-identified, free, US, person-level data found with a true 12-month prospective outcome | [MEPS](https://meps.ahrq.gov) |

-| MEPS commercial-use terms are ambiguous and must be confirmed in writing with AHRQ | The data use terms say data "may not be used for any purpose other than for the purpose for which they were supplied" | [MEPS DUA wording](https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h213d/h213ddoc.shtml) |

-| Business model: sell the platform (pipeline, calibration, retraining on customer data), not trained weights alone | Reduces dependence on MEPS terms and on synthetic data realism | Earlier critique in this project |

-| NHS or UK data rejected | CPRD costs about £20,600 to £83,850 per year and limits use to public-health research ([CPRD pricing](https://www.cprd.com/access-data/pricing)). OpenSAFELY requires UK-based users and returns aggregates only ([OpenSAFELY](https://www.opensafely.org/access-to-opensafely/)). US and UK coding and care patterns differ. | Earlier research |

-| MIMIC-IV and other credentialed sets rejected for training | Require approved access and restrict use. MIMIC's agreement bans sending data to online services such as LLM APIs, which conflicts with AI-assisted development | [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/) |
-| Health and Retirement Study rejected | Restricted to research and statistical purposes | [HRS overview](https://hrs.isr.umich.edu/sites/default/files/biblio/OverviewofHRSPublicData.pdf) |
-| MCBS public file rejected | Contains no utilization data, so no hospitalization label | [CMS MCBS PUF guide](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/2021-mcbs-puf-data-user-guide.pdf) |

-| Synthea used only to test the ETL and service, never to judge accuracy | Its outcomes are simulated by rules; its realism is limited | [Synthea](https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea), [evaluation 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6416981/), [evaluation 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7651916/) |
-| CPT procedure codes are not used | CPT requires an AMA license | [AMA CPT licensing](https://www.ama-assn.org/practice-management/cpt/cpt-licensing-frequently-asked-questions-faqs) |

-| ICD-10-CM and SNOMED CT are allowed | ICD-10-CM is free in the US. SNOMED CT and the SNOMED to ICD-10-CM map are free in the US with a UMLS license | [NLM map](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/mapping_projects/snomedct_to_icd10cm.html) |

-| Regulatory posture: non-time-critical risk score shown to clinicians with its basis visible | Likely outside FDA device rules or under enforcement discretion per FDA clinical decision support guidance. Must be reviewed by counsel | [FDA CDS guidance](https://www.fda.gov/media/109618/download) |
-| Benchmark: QAdmissions (UK) reports AUROC 0.77 to 0.78 and top-decile PPV of 42% for emergency admission | Published reference point | [BMJ Open](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/3/8/e003482) |

-| Label (target) | The known outcome attached to each training example. Here `label_hosp_12m` = 1 if the person had at least one inpatient discharge in calendar year 2 of their MEPS panel (`IPDISY2 > 0`), else 0. |
-| Features (inputs) | Information from calendar year 1 only, used to predict the label. |
-| Prediction | The model's output: a probability from 0 to 1 that the label is 1. |
-| Year 1, year 2 | The two calendar years of a MEPS longitudinal panel. Panel 27 covers 2022 (year 1) and 2023 (year 2). |
-| AUROC | Probability that a random hospitalized person is ranked above a random non-hospitalized person. 0.5 is chance. |
-| AUPRC | Average precision. Chance equals the event rate (about 0.088). |
-| Brier score | Mean squared error of predicted probabilities. Lower is better. |
-| Top-decile PPV | Share hospitalized among the 10% with the highest predicted risk. |
-| Calibration | Whether predicted risks match observed rates, checked by risk deciles. |
-| Simple comparison model | Logistic regression on age and any hospital stay in year 1. Used as a baseline and shown alongside the main score. |
-- Panels 21 to 27, two-year longitudinal files only. Panel to file: 21 = HC-202, 22 = HC-210, 23 = HC-217, 24 = HC-225, 25 = HC-234, 26 = HC-244, 27 = HC-252.
-- HC-245 is a Panel 24 three-year file. It must be excluded to avoid duplicate people.
-- Population: adults 18 and older on December 31 of year 1, with non-negative `IPDISY1` and `IPDISY2`.
-- Expected result: 56,360 adults, 4,820 hospitalized in year 2 (8.6%).

-- Available but not yet used: Medical Conditions files (3-character ICD-10-CM plus CCSR categories), Prescribed Medicines files (NDC, Multum drug classes), event files (hospital stays with reason and ER flag, office visits with services), function, mental health, BMI, social needs, preventive care. Full inventory: `MEPS_feature_inventory.md`, which Claude Code should regenerate (see Developer Notes).

## Summary

Planning docs for **Phase 8: Patient Outcome Prediction**. The model is a gradient-boosting classifier that estimates an adult's probability of at least one inpatient stay in the next 12 months. It is trained on free, open AHRQ MEPS data and returns a FHIR `RiskAssessment`. Docs only, no code.

Phase 8 was seeded by a research prototype from an earlier session. Its content has been written into this repo's conventions. **The raw hand-off documents are deliberately not kept** (decision O5): they used their own "Phase" numbering and standalone-repo instructions, which would mislead future searches.

> **Merge note:** please **squash-merge**. The first commit on this branch briefly added the raw hand-off files and the second removes them. Squashing keeps them out of `main`'s history entirely.

## What's in `docs/phase8/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Canonical status statement |
| `prd.md` | Goals and non-goals; requirements, keeping the prototype's `FR-*` IDs with a status for each; acceptance criteria; §11 lists every deviation from the prototype's plan |
| `design.md` | Service layout, feature contract, `RiskAssessment` shape, training vs scoring mode, the FHIR mapping sketch, the agent's tool contract, and prototype defects found in review |
| `decisions.md` | ADR-style index `O1`–`O27` (`O` = Outcome) |
| `milestone-plan.md` | M1–M11, plus a mapping from the prototype's planned stages (described by content, not number) |
| `prototype-baseline.md` | What the prototype established: data-source choices, MEPS and Synthea facts, method and parameters, and the exact numbers M1–M3 must reproduce |

`docs/README.md` now indexes Phase 8.

## Main reconciliation decisions

- The prototype's planned stages become **milestones M1–M11 plus a deferred Phase 8b** (O4). Its stage numbers are not used anywhere.
- **One new service, `outcome-prediction-service/`** (O2). It returns a **FHIR `RiskAssessment` with `probabilityDecimal`** (O3), using Phase 8's own models. `triage-service`'s model has no numeric probability and is left unchanged.
- **Monorepo conventions replace the standalone-repo tooling** (O12):
  - Python `>=3.11`, a `phase8` compose profile, a `phase8` CI job, and the existing dev container.
  - The Phase 1 independence job is not touched.
- **Patient data comes in as FHIR from `fhir-service` through `client/clinical`, built in this phase** (O8, O9). It is coordinated with Phase 7 M3, which extends the same client.
- **Reproduce before changing anything** (O6, O7). The package is built from the method recorded in `prototype-baseline.md` and must match its numbers (56,360 rows; AUROC 0.769 and 0.708). The prototype's scripts are not committed.
- **The prototype leaks future data into its prescription-fill feature** (design §11). This is fixed with explicit `as_of` scoring and a mandatory leakage test (O10).
- **New `outcome-prediction-agent` built on `agent-platform`** (O15, O16). Its tools cannot accept feature values or thresholds, so it cannot re-score or band a result. `mcp-agent` is untouched.
- The service is internal-only, with no Kong route (O14).

## Open items

- **O23:** whether AHRQ allows commercial use of models trained on MEPS. This is a legal question and blocks commercialisation, not the build.
- **O24:** qualitative risk bands, which need clinical sign-off.
- **O25:** what to do with features that don't carry over from MEPS to FHIR or claims data.
- **O26:** whether customers will send FHIR, claims, or both.
- **O27:** who signs off the clinical code lists.

## Validation

- All relative links in `docs/phase8/` and the new `docs/README.md` entries were checked: they resolve.
- Every `prototype-baseline.md` section cited elsewhere exists.
- Every decision ID cited (`O1`–`O27`) exists in `decisions.md`.
- No references to the removed raw files remain.
- No code changed, so no tests were run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
## Critique

**The idea is right.** The plan picks "any inpatient stay" and one gradient-boosting model as fixed, but whether that's the right thing to predict is still open. O1 settles only the first outcome, and the any-stay vs unplanned-stay question is unresolved. Exploration that engineers can return to and repeat fills a real gap. Five problems with the request as phrased:

**1. A milestone you can revisit breaks how this repo uses milestones.**
- Every phase treats a milestone as a one-time deliverable that ends as "done". Status in each phase's README depends on that.
- A milestone that reopens with each round of research means "M7 done" stops meaning anything.
- Better: split it in two.
  - A **milestone that builds the tooling** once, and then completes.
  - A **standing protocol** anyone can run any number of times. Each run leaves a dated, permanent record; nothing gets reopened.
- Repo precedent: Phase 6 kept `telemetry-schema.md` as a separate, long-lived document beside its milestones.

**2. The biggest risk is overfitting the test set, not tooling.**
- Exploration that resumes forever, all scored on the same test panels (26–27), slowly tunes everything to those panels. Each look is harmless; hundreds of looks are not.
- The tools have to enforce a rule:
  - exploration scores itself only by cross-validation within panels 21–25;
  - the test panels are opened only to confirm a candidate already chosen, and every opening is logged.
- When AHRQ releases a newer panel, it becomes a fresh, untouched test set.
- Without this rule, more exploration makes the results less trustworthy, not more.

**3. Which predictions are advisable isn't purely an ML question.** A model that scores well can still be the wrong product. Each candidate needs a scorecard with non-ML criteria:
- **Measurable in customer data:** can the outcome be seen in FHIR or claims data? If not, it can never be validated or recalibrated for a customer.
- **Actionable:** can a care manager do anything about it?
- **Base rate:** how common is the outcome?
- **Lead time:** how far ahead does the prediction come?
- **Fairness.**
- **Regulatory position:** whether the FDA would treat the score as a medical device.

The space of possible outcomes is also limited to labels MEPS actually contains. Plausible candidates, all to be confirmed against the files:

| Candidate | Type of prediction |
|---|---|
| Any stay | Yes/no |
| Unplanned stay | Yes/no |
| ED visits | Count |
| High-cost member (e.g. top 10% of spending) | Yes/no |
| Nights in hospital | Count |

One thing to state honestly: what care managers most want is a prediction of **who will benefit from outreach** (in ML terms, uplift or "impactability"). MEPS has no intervention data, so that can't be built here. The tools should record that limit, not imply it's covered.

**4. "Exploration tools" isn't the industry term, and the risk is over-building.**
- The standard terms:
  - **Experiment tracking:** a record of every run's config, data checksums, code commit, seed and metrics.
  - A **model registry:** candidates with a promotion stage.
  - **Model cards:** a standard summary sheet published with each promoted model.
- The standard open-source tool is **MLflow**:
  - Apache 2.0 licence, runs entirely locally on file or SQLite storage.
  - Has a browsing UI.
  - Fits the "nothing leaves this machine" rule.
- Alternatives:
  - **DVC** is more git-native but weaker for browsing results.
  - **Weights & Biases** is a hosted (SaaS) service, so I'd reject it: it sends data off the machine.
- Don't build a platform (feature store, pipeline orchestrator). CLAUDE.md asks for the smallest useful solution:
  - MLflow running locally;
  - experiment configs plus a command-line tool;
  - a protocol document;
  - a scorecard template.

**5. It needs a defined path into production, or exploration quietly changes it.**
- Results must move through explicit stages: experiment → candidate (scorecard + model card) → a new feature-contract version plus a decision entry → served by the service.
- The service never loads anything that skipped those stages. This matches the rule already in place that a new contract version is never an edit to an existing one.

**Smaller points**
- **Notebooks:** allowed for exploring, but stored with outputs stripped. Experiments that count must be scripted and configured so others can repeat them.
- **Separate package:** a new top-level `outcome-prediction-lab/`, so MLflow and research-only dependencies stay out of the scoring service's runtime.
- **Name:** `-lab` is a common industry label for this kind of workspace; `outcome-prediction-experiments/` is the more literal option.
- **Sequencing:** build the tooling right after M2 (the reproduced baseline), alongside the service work. M9 (unplanned-stay label) and M10 (features and tuning) then become the **first two runs of the protocol**, rather than one-off code. That's less code overall.

## What I'd write, if you agree

- A new milestone, **"Experimentation workbench"**, placed after M2:
  - MLflow tracking and a model registry, stored locally and gitignored;
  - a command-line tool that runs experiments from config files, with the test-set rule built in;
  - a scorecard for comparing prediction targets;
  - a model-card template;
  - a first exploration that compares the candidate outcomes above.
- `docs/phase8/experimentation-protocol.md`: the runbook for any future round. It covers how to start a round, the test-set rules, the promotion stages, and how to record the result.
- M9 and M10 rewritten as rounds of that protocol.
- Remaining milestones renumbered.
- New decision entries in `decisions.md`:
  - MLflow chosen over DVC and W&B;
  - the test-set access rule;
  - the promotion stages;
  - research dependencies kept in a separate package;
  - uplift recorded as out of reach with MEPS.

Two choices before I write:

1. **Package name:** `outcome-prediction-lab` or `outcome-prediction-experiments`?
2. **Scope of "types of prediction":**
   - (a) only which outcome to predict, from the MEPS candidates above; or
   - (b) also the form of the prediction, e.g. a yes/no probability vs a count (how many ED visits) vs a cost estimate.

   (b) is broader and costs about one extra exploration round.

Answers:

1: outcome-prediction-lab
2: (b), the broader one that deserves more work|

# Phase 8 Experimentation Protocol — Running a Research Round

The standing procedure for exploring models and prediction targets with
`outcome-prediction-lab/`. It applies to **every** round, by anyone, at any time, long after
Phase 8's milestones are complete (`decisions.md` O28). Milestone M3 builds the tooling this
document refers to; M10 and M11 are the first two rounds run under it.

> **This document is a runbook, not a status page.** Phase 8's status lives in
> [`README.md`](./README.md); a round's results live in its own committed directory (§3).
> If a step below no longer matches the tooling, fix this document in the same change.

---

## 1. When to start a round

Start a round when there's a question the current model can't answer with a number already
on record. Typical triggers:

- A new outcome or prediction form is worth evaluating (O34).
- A new feature group, label definition or model family is proposed.
- AHRQ publishes a new MEPS panel (also triggers a holdout rotation — §5).
- A customer's data shows a feature isn't portable (O25) and an alternative is needed.
- A served model's assumptions are questioned (fairness, calibration, a subgroup).

Don't start a round to tune a number nobody has asked about.

## 2. The rules every round follows

1. **Training panels only for exploration.** All comparisons use panel-grouped cross-validation
   within training panels (21–25 today). Never select, tune or compare on the test panels (O32).
2. **The test set is for confirmation, and every look is logged.** Opening the test panels
   requires a candidate named *before* the look and an appended entry in the holdout ledger
   (§5). The CLI enforces this; don't work around it.
3. **Only config-driven runs count.** A notebook can suggest an idea; a result in a round report
   must come from a committed config re-runnable with the lab's CLI (O38).
4. **Public data only.** MEPS public files and Synthea. No customer data, no PHI, nothing sent
   to an online service (prd §4, O16).
5. **Reproduce before you compare.** Each round re-runs the current served model's config first,
   so its baseline numbers come from the same code and library versions as the new ones.
6. **Synthea is never evidence of accuracy.** It may appear only as a pipeline check.

## 3. Steps

1. **Open the round.** Create `outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/NNN-<slug>/` (next free number)
   with a `README.md` stating the question, the candidates, the success criteria and which
   test-panel confirmation (if any) is planned. Commit it before running anything — the
   pre-registration.
2. **Write configs.** One config per candidate under the round's `configs/`: label definition,
   prediction form, feature set (contract version), model family and hyperparameter search
   space, seeds.
3. **Run.** Execute the configs with the lab CLI. Runs are tracked in the local MLflow store
   (O30) with data checksums, code commit, config, seed, metrics and artifacts.
4. **Compare on cross-validation.** Use the lab's comparison report. Look at subgroups and
   calibration, not only AUROC.
5. **Fill the scorecard.** For each serious candidate, complete the target scorecard (§4) —
   ML criteria from the runs, non-ML criteria by a person with written rationale.
6. **Confirm (optional, logged).** For at most the candidates named in step 1, append to the
   holdout ledger and run the test-panel evaluation.
7. **Write the round report.** `report.md` in the round directory: question, what was run,
   cross-validated results, scorecards, any confirmation results, conclusion, and what's left
   open. Export summary metrics to `metrics.json` beside it.
8. **Decide.** A round ends in one of: *no change*; *candidate* (with model card, O39) awaiting
   promotion; or *recommend promotion*, which needs a new `decisions.md` entry (§6).
9. **Commit** the round directory, ledger entries and any protocol fixes together.

## 4. The target scorecard (O36)

| Criterion | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Discrimination (AUROC/AUPRC, or the form's equivalent) | CV runs | With bootstrap intervals |
| Calibration | CV runs | By decile; mean predicted vs actual |
| Subgroup performance and fairness | CV runs | Age band, sex, prior use, race/ethnicity, insurance |
| Base rate | Data | Very rare outcomes make poor worklists |
| Measurable in FHIR / claims | Person | Can a customer's own data observe this outcome? If not: no validation, no recalibration |
| Actionable for care management | Person | What would a care manager do differently? |
| Lead time | Person | Is there time to act before the outcome? |
| FHIR representability | Person | Probability → `RiskAssessment` natively; count/cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35) |
| Regulatory posture | Person | Does this change the FDA CDS position? |
| Uplift / impactability | — | Always "not assessable with MEPS" (O37) |

## 5. The holdout ledger and rotation (O32)

`outcome-prediction-lab/holdout-ledger.md` is append-only: date, round, candidate config, who,
and why the look was needed. The lab CLI refuses a test-panel evaluation unless the candidate
has a ledger entry.

**Rotation.** When AHRQ releases a newer two-year longitudinal panel: it becomes the
confirmation set; the previous test panels join the training panels; the ledger records the
rotation; and the next round re-establishes the served model's baseline on the new split.

## 6. Promotion (O33)

A candidate reaches production only by: a round report recommending it → a model card → a new
`decisions.md` entry (and, for a non-probability form, the O35 decision) → a new contract or
target version → an artifact carrying a promotion record. `outcome-prediction-service` refuses
artifacts without one. The first promotion is milestone M12; later promotions follow the same
steps without a new milestone.

## 7. Resuming after a long gap

1. Read the latest round reports in `outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/` and the holdout ledger.
2. Re-run the served model's config and confirm its recorded numbers (§2 rule 5). If they
   moved, find out why before anything else — library versions are the usual cause.
3. Check whether AHRQ has published new panels (§5).
4. Open a new round.

# Phase 8 Experimentation Protocol — Running a Research Round

The standing procedure for exploring models and prediction targets with
`outcome-prediction-lab/`. It applies to **every** round, by anyone, at any time, long after
Phase 8's milestones are complete (`decisions.md` O28). Milestone M3 builds the tooling this
document refers to; M10 and M11 are the first two rounds run under it.

> **This document is a runbook, not a status page.** Phase 8's status lives in
> [`README.md`](./README.md); a round's results live in its own committed directory (§3).
> If a step below no longer matches the tooling, fix this document in the same change.

---

## 1. When to start a round

Start a round when there's a question the current model can't answer with a number already
on record. Typical triggers:

- A new outcome or prediction form is worth evaluating (O34).
- A new feature group, label definition or model family is proposed.
- AHRQ publishes a new MEPS panel (also triggers a holdout rotation — §5).
- A customer's data shows a feature isn't portable (O25) and an alternative is needed.
- A served model's assumptions are questioned (fairness, calibration, a subgroup).

Don't start a round to tune a number nobody has asked about.

## 2. The rules every round follows

1. **Training panels only for exploration.** All comparisons use panel-grouped cross-validation
   within training panels (21–25 today). Never select, tune or compare on the test panels (O32).
2. **The test set is for confirmation, and every look is logged.** Opening the test panels
   requires a candidate named *before* the look and an appended entry in the holdout ledger
   (§5). The CLI enforces this; don't work around it.
3. **Only config-driven runs count.** A notebook can suggest an idea; a result in a round report
   must come from a committed config re-runnable with the lab's CLI (O38).
4. **Public data only.** MEPS public files and Synthea. No customer data, no PHI, nothing sent
   to an online service (prd §4, O16).
5. **Reproduce before you compare.** Each round re-runs the current served model's config first,
   so its baseline numbers come from the same code and library versions as the new ones.
6. **Synthea is never evidence of accuracy.** It may appear only as a pipeline check.

## 3. Steps

1. **Open the round.** Create `outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/NNN-<slug>/` (next free number)
   with a `README.md` stating the question, the candidates, the success criteria and which
   test-panel confirmation (if any) is planned. Commit it before running anything — the
   pre-registration.
2. **Write configs.** One config per candidate under the round's `configs/`: label definition,
   prediction form, feature set (contract version), model family and hyperparameter search
   space, seeds.
3. **Run.** Execute the configs with the lab CLI. Runs are tracked in the local MLflow store
   (O30) with data checksums, code commit, config, seed, metrics and artifacts.
4. **Compare on cross-validation.** Use the lab's comparison report. Look at subgroups and
   calibration, not only AUROC.
5. **Fill the scorecard.** For each serious candidate, complete the target scorecard (§4) —
   ML criteria from the runs, non-ML criteria by a person with written rationale.
6. **Confirm (optional, logged).** For at most the candidates named in step 1, append to the
   holdout ledger and run the test-panel evaluation.
7. **Write the round report.** `report.md` in the round directory: question, what was run,
   cross-validated results, scorecards, any confirmation results, conclusion, and what's left
   open. Export summary metrics to `metrics.json` beside it.
8. **Decide.** A round ends in one of: *no change*; *candidate* (with model card, O39) awaiting
   promotion; or *recommend promotion*, which needs a new `decisions.md` entry (§6).
9. **Commit** the round directory, ledger entries and any protocol fixes together.

## 4. The target scorecard (O36)

| Criterion | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Discrimination (AUROC/AUPRC, or the form's equivalent) | CV runs | With bootstrap intervals |
| Calibration | CV runs | By decile; mean predicted vs actual |
| Subgroup performance and fairness | CV runs | Age band, sex, prior use, race/ethnicity, insurance |
| Base rate | Data | Very rare outcomes make poor worklists |
| Measurable in FHIR / claims | Person | Can a customer's own data observe this outcome? If not: no validation, no recalibration |
| Actionable for care management | Person | What would a care manager do differently? |
| Lead time | Person | Is there time to act before the outcome? |
| FHIR representability | Person | Probability → `RiskAssessment` natively; count/cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35) |
| Regulatory posture | Person | Does this change the FDA CDS position? |
| Uplift / impactability | — | Always "not assessable with MEPS" (O37) |

## 5. The holdout ledger and rotation (O32)

`outcome-prediction-lab/holdout-ledger.md` is append-only: date, round, candidate config, who,
and why the look was needed. The lab CLI refuses a test-panel evaluation unless the candidate
has a ledger entry.

**Rotation.** When AHRQ releases a newer two-year longitudinal panel: it becomes the
confirmation set; the previous test panels join the training panels; the ledger records the
rotation; and the next round re-establishes the served model's baseline on the new split.

## 6. Promotion (O33)

A candidate reaches production only by: a round report recommending it → a model card → a new
`decisions.md` entry (and, for a non-probability form, the O35 decision) → a new contract or
target version → an artifact carrying a promotion record. `outcome-prediction-service` refuses
artifacts without one. The first promotion is milestone M12; later promotions follow the same
steps without a new milestone.

## 7. Resuming after a long gap

1. Read the latest round reports in `outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/` and the holdout ledger.
2. Re-run the served model's config and confirm its recorded numbers (§2 rule 5). If they
   moved, find out why before anything else — library versions are the usual cause.
3. Check whether AHRQ has published new panels (§5).
4. Open a new round.

**Deliverable:** The e2e suite passes; demo steps documented in `docs/demo-guide.md`.

**Depends on:** M8.

---

### M10 — Round 001: what to predict, and in what form

**Short story:** The first real research round — decide which outcomes and prediction forms
are advisable, by scorecard, not by metric alone.

**Long story:** Run under the protocol (pre-registered in
`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-target-study/`). Candidates span outcome × form (O34): any
inpatient stay (the baseline), **unplanned stay** (excluding childbirth/pregnancy, `RSNINHOS`
4/5/6, optionally planned stays — FR-D4, `prototype-baseline.md` §8), ED visits, hospital
nights and high cost; forms of event probability, expected count, cost and ordinal tier where
they apply. Round-3 items excluded or tested separately (FR-D7). Re-run the 18–44 sex check that
exposed the childbirth problem (7.4% vs 2.2%). Every serious candidate gets a full scorecard
(O36) — including measurability in FHIR/claims, actionability, FHIR representability (O35),
and the explicit uplift gap (O37). Confirmation on the test panels only for the named
finalists, through the ledger.

**Deliverable:** Round report with scorecards and model cards; O40 decided — which
outcome(s) and form(s) to take forward — as a new `decisions.md` entry; for any
non-probability form chosen, the O35 representation decision too.

**Depends on:** M3.

---

### M11 — Round 002: improve the chosen target(s)

**Short story:** Close the gap to the prototype's targets (AUROC ≥ 0.78; ≥ 0.73 for 65+) for
what M10 chose.

**Long story:** Run under the protocol. FR-D5 (condition/CCSR and drug-class features from
MEPS event files), FR-D6 as a separately reported survey-only experiment, FR-M5 (hyperparameter
search via the lab's panel-grouped CV), FR-M6 (65+), FR-E6 (fairness by race/ethnicity and
insurance). Decide O25 (non-portable features) with numbers. Any feature that can't be derived
from FHIR stays out of the servable contract.

**Deliverable:** Round report; a candidate with model card, recommended for promotion as a new
contract version; O25 recorded in `decisions.md`.

**Depends on:** M10.

---

### M12 — First promotion into the service

**Short story:** Exercise the promotion path end to end, once, so it's proven before anyone
relies on it.

**Long story:** `promote.py` writes `PROMOTION.json` (O33, `design.md` §8); the service
starts refusing artifacts without it, and the `meps25-v1` artifact gets its retrofitted record.
Serve M11's candidate as a new contract/target version beside `meps25-v1`: FHIR extractor and
`to_contract.py` extended for its features, `RiskAssessment` outcome coding and window updated
for its target, the agent's narration checked against it, M9's acceptance case extended. If M10
chose a non-probability form, implement the representation O35 decided.

**Deliverable:** Both versions servable; an unpromoted artifact is refused (tested); the e2e
suite passes for the new version.

**Depends on:** M7 (service), M11 (candidate).

---

### M13 — Versioned clinical code lists

**Short story:** Replace description regexes with reviewed ICD-10-CM code lists.

**Long story:** FR-T4: SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM via the NLM map (UMLS licence, free in the US —
an account the repo owner holds, not a repo secret), truncated to 3 characters, one versioned
list per diagnosis flag under `etl/codelists/`. `data/reference/icd10/` is reused where it
covers the need. Lists ship marked "unreviewed" until O27 has an owner.

**Deliverable:** Both extractors use the code lists; the parity and `coronary` regression tests
still pass; flag prevalence on Synthea compared before/after in the data-quality report.

**Depends on:** M6.

---

## What's explicitly not a milestone here

Per `prd.md` §8: cloud deployment, recalibration on customer data, monitoring, population batch
from object storage, first customer validation (all **Phase 8b**); a shared or hosted
experiment-tracking server (Phase 8b); a claims-file adapter; persisting `RiskAssessment` to
`fhir-service`; a Kong route; a worklist UI; qualitative risk bands; uplift/impactability
modelling (O37). Future research rounds and promotions after M12 are protocol runs, not
milestones (O28). None of these gets a milestone number; adding one later is a new decision,
not an oversight in this plan.

content.text:
I've added both answers to PR #65 as commit `9dc7b84b` on `docs/phase8-outcome-prediction-planning`. The package is `outcome-prediction-lab`, and the exploration covers both what to predict and in what form. Phase 8 now has 13 milestones in three tracks.

## Phase 8 milestones

**Baseline track: reproduce the prototype exactly**

- **M1. Service scaffold and MEPS dataset.** Create `outcome-prediction-service/` with its CI job, compose profile and test entry. Download and checksum the seven MEPS panels and rebuild the training table. It must produce exactly 56,360 adults and 4,820 hospitalizations, matching the prototype panel by panel.
- **M2. Training, evaluation, model files.** Rebuild the main model and the simple comparison model. They must score within the prototype's tolerances (0.769 and 0.708 AUROC). Write the evaluation reports and save both models with a checksum list that the service verifies before loading.

**Research track: the lab, then its first rounds**

- **M3. Experimentation workbench (`outcome-prediction-lab`).** Built once, used forever. It provides:
  - experiment tracking and a model registry with MLflow, running locally;
  - runs defined by config files, scored only by cross-validation on the training panels;
  - a holdout ledger, and a command-line tool that refuses to test on the test panels without a ledger entry;
  - a target scorecard and model cards.

  A first "round 000" re-runs M2's model through the lab and must match its numbers, proving the tools work.
- **M10. Round 001: what to predict, and in what form.** Compares outcomes (any stay, unplanned stay without childbirth, ED visits, hospital nights, high cost) across forms (probability, expected count, cost estimate, tiers). Every serious candidate is judged on the scorecard, not just on metrics. Ends with a recorded decision on what to take forward.
- **M11. Round 002: improve the chosen target(s).** Adds condition and drug features, tunes the model, looks closely at adults 65+, and checks fairness. Also decides whether to keep the spending, prescription and home-health features, which don't carry over well to customer data.
- **M12. First promotion into the service.** Runs the full path from research to production once, so it's proven before anyone relies on it. The improved model is served alongside the original. From then on, the service refuses any model that has no promotion record tied to a recorded decision.

**Service track: runs in parallel with research after M2**

- **M4. Synthea harness, scoring mode, leakage test.** First reproduce the prototype's Synthea conversion as it is. Then add scoring "as of" a date, and fix the bug where future prescription data leaked into the features. The new test must fail on the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- **M5. Extend the shared FHIR client.** Add encounters, medication history and cost data to `client/clinical` without changing anything existing code sees. Coordinated with Phase 7's planned change to the same client.
- **M6. FHIR extractor, parity check, data-quality report.** Build the model's inputs from `fhir-service`. Confirm the rough FHIR-to-input mapping against real Synthea output, and prove the FHIR path and the CSV path produce the same inputs for the same patients.
- **M7. Scoring service returning `RiskAssessment`.** The API: score a patient by ID or score pre-built input rows. Each result includes the probability, the comparison score, a percentile, the main reasons, and links to the source records.
- **M8. `outcome-prediction-agent`.** Lets a clinician ask about risk in plain language. It can only fetch and explain results. Tests check that it refuses attempts to "adjust" a score or label it "high risk".
- **M9. End-to-end acceptance test and demo.** Everything runs live under the `phase8` profile. One demo step shows that adding a record dated after the as-of date doesn't change the score.

**Close-out**

- **M13. Versioned clinical code lists.** Replace the text matching on diagnosis descriptions with reviewed ICD-10-CM code lists.

**Deferred to Phase 8b, not milestones:** cloud deployment, recalibration on customer data, monitoring, batch scoring of a whole population, a shared experiment-tracking server, and first customer validation. Research after M12 continues as new rounds, not new milestones.

## What changed in the docs

- **New:** `experimentation-protocol.md`, the permanent guide for running or resuming a research round. It covers the rules, steps, scorecard, holdout ledger, promotion, and how to resume after a long gap.
- **`decisions.md`:** new decisions O28–O40. Among them:
  - MLflow over DVC and hosted trackers;
  - the test-set access rule;
  - the promotion path;
  - serving a count or cost needs its own decision, because `RiskAssessment` only carries probabilities;
  - uplift (who benefits from outreach) recorded as out of reach with MEPS.

  O40, which outcome and form to promote first, stays open until M10.
- **`prd.md`:** two new goals, a new set of experimentation requirements, two new acceptance criteria, and a note on how the critique shaped this.
- **`design.md`:** a new section describing the lab.
- **Milestone references** were renumbered across all Phase 8 docs. The renumbering also changed some requirement IDs by mistake (for example `FR-M3` became `FR-M4`); I caught and fixed that before committing.

**Checks:** all relative links resolve, decision IDs run continuously O1–O40, and no stale milestone ranges remain. No code changed, so no tests were run.

I also removed the PR's "please squash-merge" note. It's no longer needed, since the branch history no longer contains the raw files.

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin

      - name: Test rxclaim-emulator
        run: mvn -B -f rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml test
      - name: Test claims-service
        run: mvn -B -f claims-service/pom.xml test

  # ── Phase 2 explanation agent ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  phase2-python:
    name: phase2 (python)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install and test claims-agent
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e "claims-agent[dev]"
          pytest claims-agent/tests -q

  # ── Phase 3 Python services/agents ──────────────────────────────────────────
  # A real Postgres service container so the DB-backed tests actually run here, not just
  # self-skip -- this is the executed cloud/DB smoke test M7 named as its own deliverable
  # (design.md §13), not left as a manual-only check. The groundedness eval
  # (provider-search-agent/tests/test_groundedness_eval.py) self-skips in CI: it makes
  # real, billed Claude API calls, and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/CLAUDE_API_KEY secret is
  # configured here -- a deliberate cost-conscious choice, not an oversight (design.md §13).
  phase3-python:
    name: phase3 (python)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install Phase 3 packages
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e "provider-registry-service[dev]" -e "provider-curation-agent[dev]" \
                      -e "provider-mcp-server[dev]" -e "provider-search-agent[dev]"
      - name: Check for repo-wide test-filename collisions (design.md §14, decisions.md P15)
        run: |
          dupes=$(find . -name "test_*.py" | xargs -n1 basename | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1>1')
          if [ -n "$dupes" ]; then echo "Duplicate test filenames found:"; echo "$dupes"; exit 1; fi
      - name: Run Phase 3 test suites (DB-backed tests run for real against the postgres service)
        run: |
          pytest provider-registry-service/src/provider_registry/tests \
                 provider-curation-agent/tests \
                 provider-mcp-server/tests \
                 provider-search-agent/tests \
                 data/scripts/provider_ingest -q

  # ── Phase 3 Terraform stubs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # `terraform validate` only -- not `plan` or `apply`. Plan needs live GCP provider
  # credentials this project doesn't provision (verified, not assumed: the google provider
  # authenticates during plan even for pure resource creation). Validate needs no
  # credentials and no network access to GCP, so it's the real, zero-cost, executed check
  # that's actually achievable here -- named explicitly as such rather than overclaiming a
  # `plan` this job can't actually do for free.
  phase3-terraform:
