gh pr create --base main --head feature/phase8-m3-round-001 --title "feat(phase8): M3 round 001 — outcome-prediction-lab, what to predict and how" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Summary

The first iteration of **M3**: a new `outcome-prediction-lab` package and **round 001**. M10 and M11 are folded into M3 (O45). Full results are in [`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-what-and-how/report.md`](outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-what-and-how/report.md).

**Method:**
- Every choice was made on leave-one-panel-out cross-validation within panels 21–25.
- Test panels 26–27 were scored **once**, for **pre-registered finalists**, each logged in `holdout-ledger.md` before scoring. The code refuses to score any candidate without a ledger entry.

## Results (test panels 26–27)

| | AUROC | AUPRC | Top-10% PPV |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prototype (reproduced exactly) | 0.769 | 0.265 | 29.3% |
| **New, portable** | **0.788** (+0.019, CI +0.011 to +0.027) | **0.307** | **33.1%** |

**Most of the gain comes from code features (TF-IDF compressed with LSA), and mostly from pregnancy codes predicting childbirth admissions.** On non-obstetric admissions, and among men, those features add only about +0.002. So the round recommends **non-obstetric admission** (test AUROC 0.795) as the headline label (O47).

**Seven new targets**, all beating simple baselines on test:

| Target | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Non-obstetric admission | AUROC 0.795 | 0.756 |
| Admission via the ER | AUROC 0.788 | 0.754 |
| Any ED visit | AUROC 0.739 | 0.682 |
| ED visit count | Spearman 0.30 | 0.22 |
| High-cost member | AUROC 0.850 | 0.826 |
| Spending | Spearman 0.74 | 0.68 |
| Death (learning only, O48) | AUROC 0.881 | 0.859 |
| Loss of insurance (learning only, O48) | AUROC 0.871 | 0.798 |

**Concept verdicts:**

| Concept | Verdict |
|---|---|
| TF-IDF / LSA code features | **Useful** |
| Autoencoder and denoising autoencoder | About as good as LSA, at 8× the cost |
| Random forest | Same as gradient boosting |
| Knowledge scores (frailty, Charlson, Elixhauser) | Small gain |
| Tuning; monotonic constraints | Negligible |
| Honest missing-value encoding plus **missingness augmentation** | Fully fixes production-like gaps in income and spending |
| SHAP per-patient narratives, traced to the patient's own codes | **Useful** |
| Single decision tree | Costs 0.056 AUROC for readability |

## Data

- **21 more MEPS files** pinned in the manifest:
  - medical conditions and prescribed medicines for each panel's first year (2016–2022);
  - inpatient stays for each panel's second year (2017–2023).
- Each file was verified by its contents: the year-suffixed weight variable and the panels it holds.
- The 2016 prescriptions file exists only as SAS transport, at a URL without the usual folder. `manifest.py` and `download.py` now support this, and file IDs with a letter suffix (e.g. `239a`).

## Bugs found and fixed during the round

- **MEPS person-ID format drift.** Older files use 8 digits; newer ones add a 2-digit panel prefix. Before normalising, Panel 22 silently had no condition or drug codes.
- **A survey instrument change.** Panel 21 used the SF-12v2 rather than the VR-12, so those scores are treated as missing rather than mixed. Adult BMI was dropped: it's absent from four panels.
- **An evaluation bug** in my own code: the missingness hooks weren't passed, which made it look as if hiding values had no effect. Caught because the results were identical to four decimals; fixed and re-run.

## Housekeeping

- The frailty, Charlson and Elixhauser tables are **vendored from comorbidipy** (MIT, attributed in `NOTICE`). The library itself no longer imports under pandas 3.
- **MLflow** uses a local SQLite store and is an optional `tracking` extra (O46). MLflow 3 retired the file store.
- **Service test changes:** the manifest tests and the emulator-bucket fixture are scoped to the 7 longitudinal panels, so CI doesn't download about 95 MB of extra event files.
- **Lab unit tests** are added to the `phase8` CI job and to `pytest.ini`. Install lines updated in `CLAUDE.md` and `.ona`.
- **Docs:** decisions O45–O48; milestone plan and status updated.

## Tests

- Service: **92 passed**.
- Lab: **11 passed**.
- No duplicate test filenames.
- No data, model or tracking-database files committed. The fitted model is in the gitignored `models/`.

## Not yet built (later iterations)

- The `run / compare / confirm / card / promote` CLI (a round script stands in for now).
- The scorecard and model-card generators.
- The notebook output check.
- Round 000.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

| Death (learning only, O48) | AUROC 0.881 | 0.859 |

**Concept verdicts:**

| Concept | Verdict |
|---|---|
| TF-IDF / LSA code features | **Useful** |
| Autoencoder and denoising autoencoder | About as good as LSA, at 8× the cost |
| Random forest | Same as gradient boosting |
| Knowledge scores (frailty, Charlson, Elixhauser) | Small gain |
| Tuning; monotonic constraints | Negligible |
| Honest missing-value encoding plus **missingness augmentation** | Fully fixes production-like gaps in income and spending |
| SHAP per-patient narratives, traced to the patient's own codes | **Useful** |
| Single decision tree | Costs 0.056 AUROC for readability |

## Data

- **21 more MEPS files** pinned in the manifest:

content.text:
Iteration 1 is done and is in PR #71 (https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/71). Every choice was made by cross-validation within training panels 21–25. The untouched test panels (26–27) were scored once, for 11 finalists named in advance and logged in the holdout ledger first. The full write-up is in `outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-what-and-how/report.md`.

## 1. What to predict, beyond the prototype

Rates are for year 2:

| Target | Rate | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Non-obstetric admission** | 7.9% | The prototype's label counts childbirth. This one means what a care manager means. **Recommended as the headline label.** |
| Admission via the ER | 4.9% | The closest MEPS gets to "unplanned" |
| Any ED visit; number of ED visits | 15.5%; mean 0.24 | The same question predicted two ways: yes/no, and as a count |
| High-cost member; total spending | top 10%; mean $9,783 | Budgeting and risk contracts; yes/no and as a spending estimate |
| Death; loss of insurance | 1.1%; 1.0% | **Learning only.** Never to be promoted to the service from MEPS-only work. |

## 2. The prototype's objective: how much better

Same people, same split; the prototype reproduces exactly at 0.769:

| | AUROC | AUPRC | Top-10% PPV | Top-10% catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prototype | 0.769 | 0.265 | 29% | 33% of admissions |
| **New model** | **0.788** (+0.019, 95% CI +0.011 to +0.027) | **0.307** | **33%** | **38%** |

**But most of that gain is the model spotting pregnancies.** Year-1 codes such as Z34 ("supervision of normal pregnancy") predict childbirth admissions the following year. On non-obstetric admissions, and among men, the code features add only about +0.002. The 65+ group is barely helped: +0.010, and the confidence interval includes zero.

## 3. New targets: how well they perform

All beat their simple baselines on the test panels:
- **High-cost member:** AUROC 0.850 vs 0.826. The best discrimination of any target. But last year's spending alone already finds most of the biggest spenders.
- **Non-obstetric admission:** 0.795 vs 0.756.
- **Admission via the ER:** 0.788 vs 0.754.
- **Any ED visit:** 0.739 vs 0.682. The **largest gain over its baseline**; nearly half the top 10% go on to visit the ED.
- **ED visit count:** a modest ranking (Spearman 0.30).
- **Death:** 0.881, mostly explained by age.
- **Loss of insurance:** 0.871.

## 4. Your concepts: what helped

- **TF-IDF: yes, the biggest gain.** Each patient's codes treated as a document. Compressing it with LSA beat feeding it in raw. Mostly via pregnancy codes, though.
- **Autoencoders: they worked, but no better than the simpler LSA, at 8× the cost.** The denoising version added nothing.
- **Random forest: equal to gradient boosting.** Your explanation idea is a misconception for forests: a forest can't be "read" like one tree. The SHAP-based explanations, which work for both, made per-patient narratives possible. One example:

  > "Estimated 57% risk, model baseline 6%. Codes driving it: PRG029, Z34."

  That is how the pregnancy effect was caught. A single readable decision tree costs 0.056 AUROC.
- **Missing values: augmentation fixes it.** Training with values deliberately hidden fully recovered performance when income and spending were missing. Median imputation, the common default, was the worst option. The "Record household income: the estimate ranges from 23% to 28%" prompts work.
- **Feature importance:** the learned code pattern dominates, followed by age, spending, the number of body systems with conditions, and Medicare status. Every direction matches expectation.
- **Comparison concepts:**
  - The **frailty, Charlson and Elixhauser scores** helped a little: LSA learned the same signal from the raw codes.
  - **Tuning** and **monotonic constraints** made almost no difference.
  - **Survey items** added +0.003, but aren't available in medical records.

## 5. How a healthcare business could use these

- **Monthly care-management worklist** (non-obstetric admission). Care managers get the top 10%. About 3 in 10 of them would otherwise be admitted, and the list catches about 37% of all such admissions. Each name comes with templated reasons and data-gap prompts.
- **ED-diversion outreach** (any ED visit). Offer same-day access and after-hours options to likely ED users.
- **Finance and risk-contract planning** (high cost, spending). Calibrated spending estimates for sizing reserves and staffing, plus referral to complex care.
- **Learning only for now:** re-enrolment help for people likely to lose coverage, and serious-illness conversations. Both need governance before any real use.

## Changes and validation

- **New package `outcome-prediction-lab/`**: the round's report, metrics, pre-registration and holdout ledger.
- **21 more MEPS files** in the manifest, each verified by its contents.
- **Decisions O45–O48:**
  - **O45:** M10 and M11 folded into M3.
  - **O46:** MLflow uses a local SQLite store, as an optional extra.
  - **O47:** non-obstetric admission recommended as the headline label.
  - **O48:** death and loss of insurance are learning-only targets.
- **Tests:** service 92 passed, lab 11 passed. No data or model files committed.
- **Branch and commit:** `feature/phase8-m3-round-001` @ `f2b05858`. CI is running, and I'll report when it finishes.

## Problems found and fixed along the way

- **MEPS person IDs changed format over the years.** Before I normalised them, Panel 22 silently had no condition or drug codes at all.
- **One panel used a different health-survey instrument**, so its scores are treated as missing rather than mixed in.
- **A bug of mine** briefly made the missing-values test show no effect. I caught it because the numbers matched to four decimal places, fixed it and re-ran.

## Not done in this iteration

- **Lab tooling:** the planned command-line tools, the scorecard and model-card generators, and the notebook check. A round script stands in for now.
- **Drug classes** still show as numeric codes rather than names.
- **Experiments not tried yet:** TF-IDF on code descriptions, character n-grams on drug names, and "potentially preventable admissions". The last needs full ICD-10 codes, which MEPS doesn't release.

## Options for iteration 2, if you want one

1. Switch to **non-obstetric admission** and concentrate on the 65+ group.
2. **Text concepts:** TF-IDF on code descriptions, and character n-grams on drug names (which also gives the drug classes readable names).
3. **The rest of the lab tooling:** command-line tools, scorecard and model cards.
4. **A PyTorch autoencoder**, as a deeper learning exercise.

I didn't pin an older `shap`, because that would mean testing a different version from the one that produced the round's results.
- **Verified:** I rebuilt the new CI job locally in a clean Python 3.12 environment. `shap` 0.54.1 and scikit-learn 1.9.1 installed, and all 11 lab tests passed.
- **Unaffected:** none of the round 001 results. They were all produced on Python 3.12 in this workspace, and every other check on the PR passed, including `phase1`, `phase3` and the Terraform validations.

CI is re-running now. I'll report when it finishes, especially the new lab job. Iteration 2 and its options are still waiting on your decision.

35	## What Phase 8 is
36	
37	The platform's first **machine-learned** clinical capability. Given an adult patient in
38	`fhir-service` and an as-of date, estimate the probability of at least one inpatient stay in
39	the next 12 months, and return it as a FHIR `RiskAssessment` — with a simple, hand-checkable
40	comparison score beside it, a population percentile, the top contributing features, and
41	references to the FHIR resources the estimate was derived from.
...
46	
47	All model, feature and FHIR-mapping logic lives in one new service,
48	`outcome-prediction-service/` (O2). A new agent, `outcome-prediction-agent/`, built on
49	`agent-platform`, lets a clinician ask for a patient's risk in plain language — but its tools
50	can only look a patient up, fetch their `RiskAssessment`, and read the model card. **No tool
51	accepts feature values, thresholds or a model choice**, so the agent cannot re-score, adjust,
52	or band a result (`design.md` §9).
53	
54	## Research that outlives the phase
55	
56	Which outcomes are worth predicting — and as a probability, a count, a cost or a tier — is a
57	question this phase starts answering, not one it closes. `outcome-prediction-lab/` (built in
58	M3) is the permanent workbench: config-driven runs tracked in a local MLflow store, committed
59	round reports, a target scorecard that weighs measurability in customer data and actionability
60	alongside model metrics, and model cards. Two rules keep it honest: the test panels are opened
61	only for logged confirmation (O32), and nothing reaches the service without a promotion record
62	tied to a decision (O33). Later explorations are new **rounds** under
63	`experimentation-protocol.md`, never reopened milestones (O28).
64	
65	## Data that outlives its source
66	
67	The MEPS files are public and re-downloadable, but a source can go down, move, or quietly
68	republish different bytes. So the data is **pinned in git** — the committed
69	`outcome-prediction-service/meps-manifest.json` records the SHA-256 of every original file,
70	documentation page and codebook — and **preserved outside it**, in write-once,
71	content-addressed private mirrors. Downloads accept only bytes that match the manifest, and
72	fall back to a mirror when AHRQ can't supply them (O41, O42; `design.md` §13). Today the
73	preserved copy is the repo owner's off-workspace `file://` mirror; the retention-protected GCS
74	bucket (`outcome-prediction-service/infra/`) is ready but deferred, with a local GCS emulator
75	standing in for testing (O43).
76	
77	## Relationship to Phase 1, 6, and 7
78	
79	Additive. `fhir-service`, `triage-service`, `mcp-agent` and the Kong gateway are unmodified;
80	the new service is internal-only (O14) and runs under its own `phase8` compose profile.
81	`client/clinical` is extended additively (M5), coordinated with Phase 7 M3, which widens the
82	same client (O9). `outcome-prediction-agent` reuses Phase 6's session, observability,
83	provider seam and output-gate pattern, with the self-hosted model as default (O15, O16).
84	The `RiskAssessment` follows `triage-service`'s resource type but adds a numeric probability,
85	using Phase 8's own models (O3).
86	
87	## Terminology
88	
89	Internal work is tracked as **milestones** (M1–M13, in `milestone-plan.md`) — never
90	"Phase 8.x", same convention as every prior phase. The prototype's own planned stages are mapped onto
91	these milestones in `milestone-plan.md` (O4); its stage numbering is not used anywhere.

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository. A Cline mirror of these
rules lives in `.clinerules` — keep the two in sync when either changes.

## What this project is

An agentic healthcare workflow platform. A clinician asks a natural-language
question; an LLM/MCP layer fetches FHIR data, evaluates clinical risk, and
returns a structured recommendation. Reference workflow: **prescription refill
risk triage** (drug-allergy conflict detection).

Request flow: **mcp-agent → triage-service → fhir-service**, fronted by a Kong
gateway. Key components:

| Path | What it is | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `fhir-service/` | HAPI FHIR JPA R4 server (H2 local, Neon PostgreSQL cloud) | Java 21 / Spring Boot |
| `triage-service/` | FastAPI service; drug-allergy rule engine → FHIR `RiskAssessment` | Python |
| `mcp-agent/` | Anthropic tool-use CLI orchestrator (**no clinical logic**) | Python |
| `client/clinical/` | Domain-abstracted FHIR client library (shared by agent + triage) | Python |
| `client/platform/` | Direct FHIR-server integration tests | Python |
| `gateway/` | Kong config (key-auth, rate limiting) for GKE | YAML / Helm |
| `data/scripts/` | Synthea data generation + demo seeding | Python |

Conventions to preserve: the agent orchestrates but holds no clinical logic
(rules live in `triage-service/src/triage/rules.py`); `client/clinical` speaks
clinical domain terms, never raw FHIR bundles; the two `client/` subfolders
serve different audiences and should not modify each other's code.

## Build & test

```
# Python packages (editable installs + test tooling — see .ona/automations.yaml)
python -m pip install -e "client/clinical[dev]" -e "agent-platform[dev]" -e "triage-service[dev]" -e "mcp-agent[dev]" -e "provider-registry-service[dev]" -e "provider-curation-agent[dev]" -e "provider-mcp-server[dev]" -e "provider-search-agent[dev]" -e "outcome-prediction-service[dev]" -e "outcome-prediction-lab[dev]"
pytest <path>                       # run focused tests for the changed package

# provider-registry-service's DB-backed tests need a local Postgres; they self-skip
# (not error) when one isn't reachable at TEST_DATABASE_URL — see
# provider-registry-service/src/provider_registry/tests/conftest.py.

# FHIR service (Java). Unset SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL / NEON_* first so tests use H2;
# otherwise MdmTest boots against a live DB and fails on auth (env issue, not code).
cd fhir-service && ./mvnw clean verify        # full build + tests
cd fhir-service && ./mvnw spring-boot:run     # run locally on :8080 (H2)
```

The mcp-agent accepts `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_API_KEY` (the Ona secret name).

Run only the tests relevant to a change when practical. Never claim tests
passed unless they actually ran; if they can't run, say why.

This project intentionally uses two Git worktrees. Treat them as independent
environments and never confuse them:

- `/workspaces/fhir-agent` — branch `main`. Application code, features, tests,
  pull requests, code review.
- `/workspaces/.ai-chat-history` — branch `ai-chat-history`. AI conversation
  archive, export scripts, archive tooling.

Before any Git write operation, briefly state: **current worktree, current
branch, intended target branch.** Refuse to run Git commands if the intended
worktree is ambiguous.

## Git rules

**Application code (`/workspaces/fhir-agent`)**
- Never commit directly to `main`.
- For any change to `main`-branch work, **default to creating a feature branch
  and opening a PR** — do this proactively without asking. Don't ask ambiguous
  "should I branch?" questions each time; just branch and push, then report.
  Only skip the branch/PR if I explicitly say to.
- Never merge branches yourself. Prepare work for GitHub review; keep the PR
  up to date as work continues.
- After a PR is merged, **always ask to delete the feature branch** — both the
  `origin` remote branch and the local branch. Delete only after I confirm, and
  never delete `main` or `ai-chat-history`.

**AI archive (`/workspaces/.ai-chat-history`)**
- Work only on `ai-chat-history`.
- Never open a PR; never merge `ai-chat-history` into `main`.
- Commit directly after successful testing and push to `origin/ai-chat-history`.
- Keep archive commits isolated from application history.

## Terminal usage

- Run one logical operation per state-changing or order-dependent step, and
  inspect its result before the next. Do **not** chain inspect + modify + test +
  commit + push into a single `&&`/`;` command.
- Batching **independent read-only** commands in one turn is fine and preferred.
- Avoid interactive commands; use non-interactive Git flags.
- If a command is denied or the UI marks it **Skipped**: stop, report it, and
  wait — never assume a skipped/denied command succeeded.

## How to work

Behave like a pragmatic senior engineer. Optimise for working software:

- Make reasonable assumptions when risk is low; state them briefly if helpful
  and continue rather than stopping for clarification.
- Implement the smallest useful solution. Don't over-engineer; avoid premature
  optimisation and unnecessary abstractions. Match the existing codebase.
- Refactor only when it clearly improves maintainability or saves real future
  effort. Don't expand scope unless asked.
- Reserve deep architectural analysis for changes that are hard to reverse or
  touch production reliability, **security, privacy, healthcare compliance, or
  data integrity.**

Stop and ask before: deleting files, destructive Git operations, changing infra
or deployment config, or modifying security-sensitive code. Protect secrets —
never expose credentials or commit sensitive information.

## Communication

Keep responses concise: briefly explain the approach, do the work, summarise the
result. Don't narrate every small action.

When work is complete, report: files changed, validation performed, branch name,
commit hash (if committed), and any known limitations.

35	## What Phase 8 is
36	
37	The platform's first **machine-learned** clinical capability. Given an adult patient in
38	`fhir-service` and an as-of date, estimate the probability of at least one inpatient stay in
39	the next 12 months, and return it as a FHIR `RiskAssessment` — with a simple, hand-checkable
40	comparison score beside it, a population percentile, the top contributing features, and
41	references to the FHIR resources the estimate was derived from.

48	`outcome-prediction-service/` (O2). A new agent, `outcome-prediction-agent/`, built on
49	`agent-platform`, lets a clinician ask for a patient's risk in plain language — but its tools
50	can only look a patient up, fetch their `RiskAssessment`, and read the model card. **No tool
51	accepts feature values, thresholds or a model choice**, so the agent cannot re-score, adjust,
52	or band a result (`design.md` §9).

55	
56	Which outcomes are worth predicting — and as a probability, a count, a cost or a tier — is a
57	question this phase starts answering, not one it closes. `outcome-prediction-lab/` (built in
58	M3) is the permanent workbench: config-driven runs tracked in a local MLflow store, committed
59	round reports, a target scorecard that weighs measurability in customer data and actionability
60	alongside model metrics, and model cards. Two rules keep it honest: the test panels are opened
61	only for logged confirmation (O32), and nothing reaches the service without a promotion record
62	tied to a decision (O33). Later explorations are new **rounds** under

"""Config-driven research runs — the engine behind the `outcome-prediction-lab` CLI.

A run is one JSON config: what to predict, from which features, with which model. `run` scores it by
leave-one-panel-out cross-validation on the training panels ONLY and writes the result next to
the config. `confirm` is the only path to the test panels, and refuses without a ledger entry.
`card`, `scorecard` and `promote` turn a confirmed run into reviewable documents and, with a
decision ID, a promotion record (decisions.md O31–O39).

    rounds/<round>/configs/<name>.json      the config (committed, written by a person)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.json         CV result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.confirm.json test-panel result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/cards/<name>.md          model card (committed)
    rounds/<round>/scorecards/<name>.md     target scorecard (committed)
    models/lab-round-<round>/<name>.joblib  fitted model (gitignored binary, O17)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

import joblib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, LogisticRegression, PoissonRegressor
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from outcome_prediction_lab import holdout
from outcome_prediction_lab.evaluate import (
    TEST_PANELS, TRAIN_PANELS, binary_metrics, cost_metrics, count_metrics, cv_predict,
)
from outcome_prediction_lab.features import FEATURE_SETS, honest_frame, make_model

LAB_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROUNDS = LAB_ROOT / "rounds"
DECISIONS = LAB_ROOT.parent / "docs" / "phase8" / "decisions.md"
# Round 001's CV-chosen gradient-boosting settings (rounds/001-what-and-how/README.md).
TUNED = {"learning_rate": 0.03, "max_leaf_nodes": 15, "min_samples_leaf": 120,
         "l2_regularization": 1.0, "max_iter": 600}
REQUIRED = {"name", "label", "task", "features", "model"}
ALLOWED = REQUIRED | {"text", "params", "monotone", "baseline_inputs", "learning_only", "description",
                      "outcome_phrase"}


class ConfigError(ValueError):
    """A config is malformed — or tries to reach the test panels."""


class PromotionRefused(PermissionError):
    """Promotion prerequisites are missing."""


# ── configs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_config(path: Path) -> dict:
    cfg = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
    if missing := REQUIRED - cfg.keys():
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: missing {sorted(missing)}")
    if unknown := cfg.keys() - ALLOWED:
        # Deliberately strict: a config can't name panels, splits or test sets at all.
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: unknown keys {sorted(unknown)} — configs choose WHAT to model; "
                          f"the split is fixed (training panels for runs, test panels only via confirm)")
    if cfg["features"] not in FEATURE_SETS:
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: features must be one of {sorted(FEATURE_SETS)}")
    if cfg["task"] not in ("binary", "count", "cost"):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: task must be binary, count or cost")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*", cfg["name"]):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: name must be lowercase letters, digits, '.' and '-'")
    return cfg


def round_dir(round_id: str) -> Path:
    d = ROUNDS / round_id
    if not d.is_dir():
        raise ConfigError(f"no round directory {d} — create it with its pre-registration README first")
    return d


def config_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    return round_dir(round_id) / "configs" / f"{name}.json"


# ── data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def lab_frame() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The honest-encoded lab table plus `desc_text` (codes as plain words). desc_text is a fixed
    lookup, not learned, so computing it outside the CV folds leaks nothing."""
    from outcome_prediction_lab.data import build_lab_table
    from outcome_prediction_lab.vocabulary import build_vocabulary, describe_tokens
    t = build_lab_table()
    h = honest_frame(t)
    vocab = build_vocabulary()
    h["desc_text"] = h["tokens"].map(lambda s: describe_tokens(s, vocab) if s else "")
    return h


def _factory(cfg: dict):
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    params = TUNED if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or {})
    return lambda: make_model(cfg["model"], cats, nums, text=cfg.get("text"), task=cfg["task"],
                              params=params, monotone=cfg.get("monotone", False))


def _baseline_factory(task: str):
    if task == "binary":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
    if task == "count":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), PoissonRegressor(alpha=1e-4, max_iter=1000))
    return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression())


def _baseline_X(df: pd.DataFrame, cols: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    X = df[cols].copy()
    X = X.fillna(X.median())
    if "totexpy1" in cols:
        X["totexpy1"] = np.log1p(X["totexpy1"].clip(lower=0))
    return X


def _targets(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict):
    raw = df[cfg["label"]].to_numpy(float)
    return (np.log1p(raw) if cfg["task"] == "cost" else raw), raw


def _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age):
    if cfg["task"] == "binary":
        return binary_metrics(y, pred, age)
    if cfg["task"] == "count":
        return count_metrics(y, pred)
    return cost_metrics(raw, pred)


def _provenance() -> dict:
    def git(*a):
        try:
            return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=LAB_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  check=True).stdout.strip()
        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            return None
    from outcome_prediction.meps.manifest import MANIFEST_PATH
    return {"at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "git_commit": git("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
            "manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256(MANIFEST_PATH.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}


# ── run / compare ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def run(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Cross-validate one config on the training panels and write runs/<name>.json."""
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    X = df[rows].reset_index(drop=True)
    y, raw = _targets(X, cfg)
    g, age = X.panel.to_numpy(), X.agey1x.to_numpy()
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = cv_predict(_factory(cfg), X, y, g, proba=proba)
    result = {"config": cfg, "cv": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        pb = cv_predict(_baseline_factory(cfg["task"]), _baseline_X(X, cfg["baseline_inputs"]), y, g, proba=proba)
        result["cv_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, age if proba else None)
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, result["cv"])
    return result


def _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, metrics):
    try:
        import mlflow
        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(f"sqlite:///{LAB_ROOT / 'mlflow.db'}")
        mlflow.set_experiment(f"round-{round_id}")
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=name):
            mlflow.log_params({k: json.dumps(v) if isinstance(v, (list, dict)) else v
                               for k, v in cfg.items() if k != "description"})
            mlflow.log_metrics({k: v for k, v in metrics.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))})
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — tracking is optional (O46)
        pass


def compare(round_id: str, metric: str | None = None) -> str:
    """A Markdown table of every run in the round, best first (writes comparison.md)."""
    runs = [json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in sorted((round_dir(round_id) / "runs").glob("*.json"))
            if not p.name.endswith(".confirm.json")]
    if not runs:
        return "_no runs yet_"
    rows = []
    for r in runs:
        cfg, cv = r["config"], r["cv"]
        key = metric or ("auroc" if cfg["task"] == "binary" else "spearman")
        base = r.get("cv_baseline", {}).get(key)
        rows.append((cfg["label"], cv.get(key, float("nan")), cfg["name"], cfg, cv, base, key))
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1]))
    lines = ["| Label | Run | Model | Text | CV metric | Value | Baseline | AUPRC / extra |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for label, val, nm, cfg, cv, base, key in rows:
        extra = f"{cv['auprc']:.3f}" if "auprc" in cv else (f"top-10% share {cv.get('top10_share_of_events', cv.get('top10_share_of_spend', float('nan'))):.3f}")
        text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "—")
        lines.append(f"| {label} | `{nm}` | {cfg['model']} | {text} | {key} | {val:.4f} | "
                     f"{'' if base is None else f'{base:.4f}'} | {extra} |")
    table = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    (round_dir(round_id) / "comparison.md").write_text(f"# Round {round_id} — cross-validated runs\n\n{table}")
    return table


# ── confirm ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fitted_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import models_dir
    return models_dir() / f"lab-round-{round_id}" / f"{name}.joblib"


def fit_on_training_panels(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None):
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    y, _ = _targets(df[rows], cfg)
    return cfg, _factory(cfg)().fit(df[rows], y)


def confirm(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """The ONE path to the test panels: refuses unless the ledger already records this look."""
    holdout.require(round_id, name)
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    cfg, model = fit_on_training_panels(round_id, name, df)
    test = df.panel.isin(TEST_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    Xt = df[test]
    y, raw = _targets(Xt, cfg)
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = model.predict_proba(Xt)[:, 1] if proba else model.predict(Xt)
    result = {"config": cfg, "test": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        train = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
        yb, _ = _targets(df[train], cfg)
        b = _baseline_factory(cfg["task"])().fit(_baseline_X(df[train], cfg["baseline_inputs"]), yb)
        Xb = _baseline_X(Xt, cfg["baseline_inputs"])
        pb = b.predict_proba(Xb)[:, 1] if proba else b.predict(Xb)
        result["test_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None)
    path = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(model, path)
    result["fitted_model_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.confirm.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    return result


# ── model card, scorecard, promotion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _load(round_id, name, kind):
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / (f"{name}.confirm.json" if kind == "confirm" else f"{name}.json")
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None


def _fmt_metrics(m: dict | None) -> str:
    if not m:
        return "_not available_"
    keys = [k for k in ("auroc", "auprc", "brier", "top10_ppv", "top10_sensitivity", "auroc_65plus",
                        "spearman", "poisson_deviance", "r2_log", "top10_share_of_events",
                        "top10_share_of_spend") if k in m]
    return ", ".join(f"{k} {m[k]:.3f}" for k in keys) + f" (n = {m['n']:,})"


def card(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    """A model card in the spirit of TRIPOD+AI: intended use, data, outcome, inputs, performance
    (CV and, if confirmed, test), limitations — generated from the committed run records."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name} — run it first")
    cfg = r["config"]

{cfg.get("description", "")}

- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.

    out = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

HUMAN_CRITERIA = {

    "actionable": "What would a care manager do differently for a flagged patient?",

def scorecard(round_id: str, name: str, criteria: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """The target scorecard (O36): ML criteria filled from the records; non-ML criteria from a
    person's JSON ({criterion: {"score": ..., "rationale": ...}}) — or marked as still owed."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name}")
    human = json.loads(Path(criteria).read_text()) if criteria else {}
    cv, base = r["cv"], r.get("cv_baseline")
    m = c["test"] if c else cv
    lines = [f"# Target scorecard — `{r['config']['label']}` via `{name}` (round {round_id})", "",
             "| Criterion | Source | Assessment |", "|---|---|---|"]
    if "auroc" in m:
        lines += [f"| Discrimination | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f}, AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f}"
                  + (f" (baseline AUROC {base['auroc']:.3f}, CV)" if base else "") + " |",
                  f"| Calibration | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Brier {m['brier']:.4f}; mean predicted {m['mean_pred']:.3f} vs rate {m['rate']:.3f} |",
                  f"| Base rate | data | {m['rate']:.1%} |",
                  f"| Worklist value | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | top 10%: {m['top10_ppv']:.0%} have the outcome; they hold {m['top10_sensitivity']:.0%} of all cases |",
                  f"| Adults 65+ | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m.get('auroc_65plus', float('nan')):.3f} |"]
    else:
        lines += [f"| Ranking | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Spearman {m['spearman']:.3f} |"]

        lines += ["", "**Learning-only target (O48): not eligible for promotion.**"]
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "scorecards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def promote(round_id: str, name: str, decision: str) -> Path:
    """Write the promotion record (O33) — only for a confirmed, carded, non-learning-only run whose
    promotion is backed by an existing decisions.md entry."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"O\d+", decision):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"decision must look like O49, got {decision!r}")
    if f"| {decision} |" not in DECISIONS.read_text():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{decision} is not in {DECISIONS} — record the decision first")

    if c is None:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no test-panel confirmation")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):

    if not card_path.exists():

        raise PromotionRefused(f"{model} does not match the model that was confirmed")

              "model_sha256": c["fitted_model_sha256"],
              "model_card_sha256": hashlib.sha256(card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    out = model.with_suffix(".PROMOTION.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return out

"""Config-driven research runs — the engine behind the `outcome-prediction-lab` CLI.

A run is one JSON config: what to predict, from which features, with which model. `run` scores it by
leave-one-panel-out cross-validation on the training panels ONLY and writes the result next to
the config. `confirm` is the only path to the test panels, and refuses without a ledger entry.
`card`, `scorecard` and `promote` turn a confirmed run into reviewable documents and, with a
decision ID, a promotion record (decisions.md O31–O39).

    rounds/<round>/configs/<name>.json      the config (committed, written by a person)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.json         CV result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.confirm.json test-panel result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/cards/<name>.md          model card (committed)
    rounds/<round>/scorecards/<name>.md     target scorecard (committed)
    models/lab-round-<round>/<name>.joblib  fitted model (gitignored binary, O17)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

import joblib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, LogisticRegression, PoissonRegressor
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from outcome_prediction_lab import holdout
from outcome_prediction_lab.evaluate import (
    TEST_PANELS, TRAIN_PANELS, binary_metrics, cost_metrics, count_metrics, cv_predict,
)
from outcome_prediction_lab.features import FEATURE_SETS, honest_frame, make_model

LAB_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROUNDS = LAB_ROOT / "rounds"
DECISIONS = LAB_ROOT.parent / "docs" / "phase8" / "decisions.md"
# Round 001's CV-chosen gradient-boosting settings (rounds/001-what-and-how/README.md).
TUNED = {"learning_rate": 0.03, "max_leaf_nodes": 15, "min_samples_leaf": 120,
         "l2_regularization": 1.0, "max_iter": 600}
REQUIRED = {"name", "label", "task", "features", "model"}
ALLOWED = REQUIRED | {"text", "params", "monotone", "baseline_inputs", "learning_only", "description",
                      "outcome_phrase"}


class ConfigError(ValueError):
    """A config is malformed — or tries to reach the test panels."""


class PromotionRefused(PermissionError):
    """Promotion prerequisites are missing."""


# ── configs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_config(path: Path) -> dict:
    cfg = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
    if missing := REQUIRED - cfg.keys():
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: missing {sorted(missing)}")
    if unknown := cfg.keys() - ALLOWED:
        # Deliberately strict: a config can't name panels, splits or test sets at all.
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: unknown keys {sorted(unknown)} — configs choose WHAT to model; "
                          f"the split is fixed (training panels for runs, test panels only via confirm)")
    if cfg["features"] not in FEATURE_SETS:
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: features must be one of {sorted(FEATURE_SETS)}")
    if cfg["task"] not in ("binary", "count", "cost"):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: task must be binary, count or cost")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*", cfg["name"]):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: name must be lowercase letters, digits, '.' and '-'")
    return cfg


def round_dir(round_id: str) -> Path:
    d = ROUNDS / round_id
    if not d.is_dir():
        raise ConfigError(f"no round directory {d} — create it with its pre-registration README first")
    return d


def config_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    return round_dir(round_id) / "configs" / f"{name}.json"


# ── data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def lab_frame() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The honest-encoded lab table plus `desc_text` (codes as plain words). desc_text is a fixed
    lookup, not learned, so computing it outside the CV folds leaks nothing."""
    from outcome_prediction_lab.data import build_lab_table
    from outcome_prediction_lab.vocabulary import build_vocabulary, describe_tokens
    t = build_lab_table()
    h = honest_frame(t)
    vocab = build_vocabulary()
    h["desc_text"] = h["tokens"].map(lambda s: describe_tokens(s, vocab) if s else "")
    return h


def _factory(cfg: dict):
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    params = TUNED if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or {})
    return lambda: make_model(cfg["model"], cats, nums, text=cfg.get("text"), task=cfg["task"],
                              params=params, monotone=cfg.get("monotone", False))


def _baseline_factory(task: str):
    if task == "binary":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
    if task == "count":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), PoissonRegressor(alpha=1e-4, max_iter=1000))
    return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression())


def _baseline_X(df: pd.DataFrame, cols: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    X = df[cols].copy()
    X = X.fillna(X.median())
    if "totexpy1" in cols:
        X["totexpy1"] = np.log1p(X["totexpy1"].clip(lower=0))
    return X


def _targets(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict):
    raw = df[cfg["label"]].to_numpy(float)
    return (np.log1p(raw) if cfg["task"] == "cost" else raw), raw


def _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age):
    if cfg["task"] == "binary":
        return binary_metrics(y, pred, age)
    if cfg["task"] == "count":
        return count_metrics(y, pred)
    return cost_metrics(raw, pred)


def _provenance() -> dict:
    def git(*a):
        try:
            return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=LAB_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  check=True).stdout.strip()
        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            return None
    from outcome_prediction.meps.manifest import MANIFEST_PATH
    return {"at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "git_commit": git("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
            "manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256(MANIFEST_PATH.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}


# ── run / compare ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def run(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Cross-validate one config on the training panels and write runs/<name>.json."""
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    X = df[rows].reset_index(drop=True)
    y, raw = _targets(X, cfg)
    g, age = X.panel.to_numpy(), X.agey1x.to_numpy()
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = cv_predict(_factory(cfg), X, y, g, proba=proba)
    result = {"config": cfg, "cv": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        pb = cv_predict(_baseline_factory(cfg["task"]), _baseline_X(X, cfg["baseline_inputs"]), y, g, proba=proba)
        result["cv_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, age if proba else None)
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, result["cv"])
    return result


def _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, metrics):
    try:
        import mlflow
        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(f"sqlite:///{LAB_ROOT / 'mlflow.db'}")
        mlflow.set_experiment(f"round-{round_id}")
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=name):
            mlflow.log_params({k: json.dumps(v) if isinstance(v, (list, dict)) else v
                               for k, v in cfg.items() if k != "description"})
            mlflow.log_metrics({k: v for k, v in metrics.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))})
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — tracking is optional (O46)
        pass


def compare(round_id: str, metric: str | None = None) -> str:
    """A Markdown table of every run in the round, best first (writes comparison.md)."""
    runs = [json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in sorted((round_dir(round_id) / "runs").glob("*.json"))
            if not p.name.endswith(".confirm.json")]
    if not runs:
        return "_no runs yet_"
    rows = []
    for r in runs:
        cfg, cv = r["config"], r["cv"]
        key = metric or ("auroc" if cfg["task"] == "binary" else "spearman")
        base = r.get("cv_baseline", {}).get(key)
        rows.append((cfg["label"], cv.get(key, float("nan")), cfg["name"], cfg, cv, base, key))
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1]))
    lines = ["| Label | Run | Model | Text | CV metric | Value | Baseline | AUPRC / extra |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for label, val, nm, cfg, cv, base, key in rows:
        extra = f"{cv['auprc']:.3f}" if "auprc" in cv else (f"top-10% share {cv.get('top10_share_of_events', cv.get('top10_share_of_spend', float('nan'))):.3f}")
        text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "—")
        lines.append(f"| {label} | `{nm}` | {cfg['model']} | {text} | {key} | {val:.4f} | "
                     f"{'' if base is None else f'{base:.4f}'} | {extra} |")
    table = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    (round_dir(round_id) / "comparison.md").write_text(f"# Round {round_id} — cross-validated runs\n\n{table}")
    return table


# ── confirm ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fitted_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import models_dir
    return models_dir() / f"lab-round-{round_id}" / f"{name}.joblib"


def fit_on_training_panels(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None):
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    y, _ = _targets(df[rows], cfg)
    return cfg, _factory(cfg)().fit(df[rows], y)


def confirm(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """The ONE path to the test panels: refuses unless the ledger already records this look."""
    holdout.require(round_id, name)
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    cfg, model = fit_on_training_panels(round_id, name, df)
    test = df.panel.isin(TEST_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    Xt = df[test]
    y, raw = _targets(Xt, cfg)
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = model.predict_proba(Xt)[:, 1] if proba else model.predict(Xt)
    result = {"config": cfg, "test": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        train = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
        yb, _ = _targets(df[train], cfg)
        b = _baseline_factory(cfg["task"])().fit(_baseline_X(df[train], cfg["baseline_inputs"]), yb)
        Xb = _baseline_X(Xt, cfg["baseline_inputs"])
        pb = b.predict_proba(Xb)[:, 1] if proba else b.predict(Xb)
        result["test_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None)
    path = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(model, path)
    result["fitted_model_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.confirm.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    return result


# ── model card, scorecard, promotion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _load(round_id, name, kind):
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / (f"{name}.confirm.json" if kind == "confirm" else f"{name}.json")
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None


def _fmt_metrics(m: dict | None) -> str:
    if not m:
        return "_not available_"
    keys = [k for k in ("auroc", "auprc", "brier", "top10_ppv", "top10_sensitivity", "auroc_65plus",
                        "spearman", "poisson_deviance", "r2_log", "top10_share_of_events",
                        "top10_share_of_spend") if k in m]
    return ", ".join(f"{k} {m[k]:.3f}" for k in keys) + f" (n = {m['n']:,})"


def card(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    """A model card in the spirit of TRIPOD+AI: intended use, data, outcome, inputs, performance
    (CV and, if confirmed, test), limitations — generated from the committed run records."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name} — run it first")
    cfg = r["config"]
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "none")
    md = f"""# Model card — `{name}` (round {round_id})

{cfg.get("description", "")}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intended use** | {"LEARNING ONLY — not for promotion (decisions.md O48)" if cfg.get("learning_only") else "Population-level planning aid for primary-care care management; not a diagnosis, not for emergencies"} |
| **Outcome** | `{cfg["label"]}` — {cfg.get("outcome_phrase", "see the round report")} (year 2 of a MEPS two-year panel) |
| **Population** | US civilian non-institutionalised adults (18+) in MEPS panels 21–27, observed in both years |
| **Training data** | Panels 21–25 (2016–2021); evaluation by leave-one-panel-out cross-validation |
| **Test data** | Panels 26–27 (2021–2023), scored once after a holdout-ledger entry |
| **Inputs** | {len(cats)} categorical + {len(nums)} numeric features (`{cfg["features"]}`); text representations: {text} |
| **Model** | `{cfg["model"]}`, task `{cfg["task"]}`, params {"round-001 tuned" if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or "defaults")} |
| **Cross-validated performance** | {_fmt_metrics(r["cv"])} |
| **Cross-validated baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(r.get("cv_baseline"))} |
| **Test performance** | {_fmt_metrics(c["test"]) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Test baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(c.get("test_baseline")) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Data provenance** | manifest sha256 `{r["provenance"]["manifest_sha256"][:12]}…`, code `{(r["provenance"]["git_commit"] or "unknown")[:12]}` |

## Limitations

- Trained on MEPS **self-reported** survey data; customer records differ (codes, charges vs payments,
  missing income). Recalibrate and validate on customer data before any use (Phase 8b).
- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.

- **Uplift / impactability is not assessable with MEPS** (no intervention data — O37): this model ranks
  risk, not who would benefit from outreach.
- Subgroup fairness by race/ethnicity and insurance is not yet reported on this card.
"""
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md)
    return out


HUMAN_CRITERIA = {
    "measurable_in_customer_data": "Can a customer's own FHIR / claims data observe this outcome (needed to validate and recalibrate)?",
    "actionable": "What would a care manager do differently for a flagged patient?",
    "lead_time": "Is there time to act before the outcome happens?",
    "fhir_representability": "Probability -> RiskAssessment natively; count / cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35).",
    "regulatory_posture": "Does this change the FDA clinical-decision-support position?",
}


def scorecard(round_id: str, name: str, criteria: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """The target scorecard (O36): ML criteria filled from the records; non-ML criteria from a
    person's JSON ({criterion: {"score": ..., "rationale": ...}}) — or marked as still owed."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name}")
    human = json.loads(Path(criteria).read_text()) if criteria else {}
    cv, base = r["cv"], r.get("cv_baseline")
    m = c["test"] if c else cv
    lines = [f"# Target scorecard — `{r['config']['label']}` via `{name}` (round {round_id})", "",
             "| Criterion | Source | Assessment |", "|---|---|---|"]
    if "auroc" in m:
        lines += [f"| Discrimination | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f}, AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f}"
                  + (f" (baseline AUROC {base['auroc']:.3f}, CV)" if base else "") + " |",
                  f"| Calibration | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Brier {m['brier']:.4f}; mean predicted {m['mean_pred']:.3f} vs rate {m['rate']:.3f} |",
                  f"| Base rate | data | {m['rate']:.1%} |",
                  f"| Worklist value | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | top 10%: {m['top10_ppv']:.0%} have the outcome; they hold {m['top10_sensitivity']:.0%} of all cases |",
                  f"| Adults 65+ | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m.get('auroc_65plus', float('nan')):.3f} |"]
    else:
        lines += [f"| Ranking | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Spearman {m['spearman']:.3f} |"]
    for key, question in HUMAN_CRITERIA.items():
        entry = human.get(key)
        cell = (f"**{entry['score']}** — {entry['rationale']}" if entry
                else f"_TO BE SCORED BY A PERSON_ — {question}")
        lines.append(f"| {key.replace('_', ' ').capitalize()} | person | {cell} |")
    lines.append("| Uplift / impactability | — | Not assessable with MEPS (no intervention data — O37) |")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        lines += ["", "**Learning-only target (O48): not eligible for promotion.**"]
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "scorecards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return out


def promote(round_id: str, name: str, decision: str) -> Path:
    """Write the promotion record (O33) — only for a confirmed, carded, non-learning-only run whose
    promotion is backed by an existing decisions.md entry."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"O\d+", decision):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"decision must look like O49, got {decision!r}")
    if f"| {decision} |" not in DECISIONS.read_text():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{decision} is not in {DECISIONS} — record the decision first")
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if c is None:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no test-panel confirmation")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} is a learning-only target (O48)")
    card_path = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    if not card_path.exists():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no model card — run `card` first")
    model = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    if hashlib.sha256(model.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != c["fitted_model_sha256"]:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{model} does not match the model that was confirmed")
    record = {"round": round_id, "run": name, "decision": decision, "label": r["config"]["label"],
              "model_sha256": c["fitted_model_sha256"],
              "model_card_sha256": hashlib.sha256(card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    out = model.with_suffix(".PROMOTION.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return out

"""Config-driven research runs — the engine behind the `outcome-prediction-lab` CLI.

A run is one JSON config: what to predict, from which features, with which model. `run` scores it by
leave-one-panel-out cross-validation on the training panels ONLY and writes the result next to
the config. `confirm` is the only path to the test panels, and refuses without a ledger entry.
`card`, `scorecard` and `promote` turn a confirmed run into reviewable documents and, with a
decision ID, a promotion record (decisions.md O31–O39).

    rounds/<round>/configs/<name>.json      the config (committed, written by a person)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.json         CV result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/runs/<name>.confirm.json test-panel result (committed)
    rounds/<round>/cards/<name>.md          model card (committed)
    rounds/<round>/scorecards/<name>.md     target scorecard (committed)
    models/lab-round-<round>/<name>.joblib  fitted model (gitignored binary, O17)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

import joblib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, LogisticRegression, PoissonRegressor
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from outcome_prediction_lab import holdout
from outcome_prediction_lab.evaluate import (
    TEST_PANELS, TRAIN_PANELS, binary_metrics, cost_metrics, count_metrics, cv_predict,
)
from outcome_prediction_lab.features import FEATURE_SETS, honest_frame, make_model

LAB_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROUNDS = LAB_ROOT / "rounds"
DECISIONS = LAB_ROOT.parent / "docs" / "phase8" / "decisions.md"
# Round 001's CV-chosen gradient-boosting settings (rounds/001-what-and-how/README.md).
TUNED = {"learning_rate": 0.03, "max_leaf_nodes": 15, "min_samples_leaf": 120,
         "l2_regularization": 1.0, "max_iter": 600}
REQUIRED = {"name", "label", "task", "features", "model"}
ALLOWED = REQUIRED | {"text", "params", "monotone", "baseline_inputs", "learning_only", "description",
                      "outcome_phrase"}


class ConfigError(ValueError):
    """A config is malformed — or tries to reach the test panels."""


class PromotionRefused(PermissionError):
    """Promotion prerequisites are missing."""


# ── configs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_config(path: Path) -> dict:
    cfg = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
    if missing := REQUIRED - cfg.keys():
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: missing {sorted(missing)}")
    if unknown := cfg.keys() - ALLOWED:
        # Deliberately strict: a config can't name panels, splits or test sets at all.
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: unknown keys {sorted(unknown)} — configs choose WHAT to model; "
                          f"the split is fixed (training panels for runs, test panels only via confirm)")
    if cfg["features"] not in FEATURE_SETS:
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: features must be one of {sorted(FEATURE_SETS)}")
    if cfg["task"] not in ("binary", "count", "cost"):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: task must be binary, count or cost")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*", cfg["name"]):
        raise ConfigError(f"{path}: name must be lowercase letters, digits, '.' and '-'")
    return cfg


def round_dir(round_id: str) -> Path:
    d = ROUNDS / round_id
    if not d.is_dir():
        raise ConfigError(f"no round directory {d} — create it with its pre-registration README first")
    return d


def config_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    return round_dir(round_id) / "configs" / f"{name}.json"


# ── data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def lab_frame() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The honest-encoded lab table plus `desc_text` (codes as plain words). desc_text is a fixed
    lookup, not learned, so computing it outside the CV folds leaks nothing."""
    from outcome_prediction_lab.data import build_lab_table
    from outcome_prediction_lab.vocabulary import build_vocabulary, describe_tokens
    t = build_lab_table()
    h = honest_frame(t)
    vocab = build_vocabulary()
    h["desc_text"] = h["tokens"].map(lambda s: describe_tokens(s, vocab) if s else "")
    return h


def _factory(cfg: dict):
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    params = TUNED if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or {})
    return lambda: make_model(cfg["model"], cats, nums, text=cfg.get("text"), task=cfg["task"],
                              params=params, monotone=cfg.get("monotone", False))


def _baseline_factory(task: str):
    if task == "binary":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
    if task == "count":
        return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), PoissonRegressor(alpha=1e-4, max_iter=1000))
    return lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression())


def _baseline_X(df: pd.DataFrame, cols: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    X = df[cols].copy()
    X = X.fillna(X.median())
    if "totexpy1" in cols:
        X["totexpy1"] = np.log1p(X["totexpy1"].clip(lower=0))
    return X


def _targets(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict):
    raw = df[cfg["label"]].to_numpy(float)
    return (np.log1p(raw) if cfg["task"] == "cost" else raw), raw


def _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age):
    if cfg["task"] == "binary":
        return binary_metrics(y, pred, age)
    if cfg["task"] == "count":
        return count_metrics(y, pred)
    return cost_metrics(raw, pred)


def _provenance() -> dict:
    def git(*a):
        try:
            return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=LAB_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  check=True).stdout.strip()
        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            return None
    from outcome_prediction.meps.manifest import MANIFEST_PATH
    return {"at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "git_commit": git("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
            "manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256(MANIFEST_PATH.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}


# ── run / compare ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def run(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Cross-validate one config on the training panels and write runs/<name>.json."""
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    X = df[rows].reset_index(drop=True)
    y, raw = _targets(X, cfg)
    g, age = X.panel.to_numpy(), X.agey1x.to_numpy()
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = cv_predict(_factory(cfg), X, y, g, proba=proba)
    result = {"config": cfg, "cv": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, age if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        pb = cv_predict(_baseline_factory(cfg["task"]), _baseline_X(X, cfg["baseline_inputs"]), y, g, proba=proba)
        result["cv_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, age if proba else None)
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, result["cv"])
    return result


def _mlflow(round_id, name, cfg, metrics):
    try:
        import mlflow
        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(f"sqlite:///{LAB_ROOT / 'mlflow.db'}")
        mlflow.set_experiment(f"round-{round_id}")
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=name):
            mlflow.log_params({k: json.dumps(v) if isinstance(v, (list, dict)) else v
                               for k, v in cfg.items() if k != "description"})
            mlflow.log_metrics({k: v for k, v in metrics.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))})
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — tracking is optional (O46)
        pass


def compare(round_id: str, metric: str | None = None) -> str:
    """A Markdown table of every run in the round, best first (writes comparison.md)."""
    runs = [json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in sorted((round_dir(round_id) / "runs").glob("*.json"))
            if not p.name.endswith(".confirm.json")]
    if not runs:
        return "_no runs yet_"
    rows = []
    for r in runs:
        cfg, cv = r["config"], r["cv"]
        key = metric or ("auroc" if cfg["task"] == "binary" else "spearman")
        base = r.get("cv_baseline", {}).get(key)
        rows.append((cfg["label"], cv.get(key, float("nan")), cfg["name"], cfg, cv, base, key))
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1]))
    lines = ["| Label | Run | Model | Text | CV metric | Value | Baseline | AUPRC / extra |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for label, val, nm, cfg, cv, base, key in rows:
        extra = f"{cv['auprc']:.3f}" if "auprc" in cv else (f"top-10% share {cv.get('top10_share_of_events', cv.get('top10_share_of_spend', float('nan'))):.3f}")
        text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "—")
        lines.append(f"| {label} | `{nm}` | {cfg['model']} | {text} | {key} | {val:.4f} | "
                     f"{'' if base is None else f'{base:.4f}'} | {extra} |")
    table = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    (round_dir(round_id) / "comparison.md").write_text(f"# Round {round_id} — cross-validated runs\n\n{table}")
    return table


# ── confirm ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fitted_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import models_dir
    return models_dir() / f"lab-round-{round_id}" / f"{name}.joblib"


def fit_on_training_panels(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None):
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    y, _ = _targets(df[rows], cfg)
    return cfg, _factory(cfg)().fit(df[rows], y)


def confirm(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """The ONE path to the test panels: refuses unless the ledger already records this look."""
    holdout.require(round_id, name)
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    cfg, model = fit_on_training_panels(round_id, name, df)
    test = df.panel.isin(TEST_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
    Xt = df[test]
    y, raw = _targets(Xt, cfg)
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    pred = model.predict_proba(Xt)[:, 1] if proba else model.predict(Xt)
    result = {"config": cfg, "test": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        train = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & df[cfg["label"]].notna().to_numpy()
        yb, _ = _targets(df[train], cfg)
        b = _baseline_factory(cfg["task"])().fit(_baseline_X(df[train], cfg["baseline_inputs"]), yb)
        Xb = _baseline_X(Xt, cfg["baseline_inputs"])
        pb = b.predict_proba(Xb)[:, 1] if proba else b.predict(Xb)
        result["test_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None)
    path = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(model, path)
    result["fitted_model_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.confirm.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    return result


# ── model card, scorecard, promotion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _load(round_id, name, kind):
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / (f"{name}.confirm.json" if kind == "confirm" else f"{name}.json")
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None


def _fmt_metrics(m: dict | None) -> str:
    if not m:
        return "_not available_"
    keys = [k for k in ("auroc", "auprc", "brier", "top10_ppv", "top10_sensitivity", "auroc_65plus",
                        "spearman", "poisson_deviance", "r2_log", "top10_share_of_events",
                        "top10_share_of_spend") if k in m]
    return ", ".join(f"{k} {m[k]:.3f}" for k in keys) + f" (n = {m['n']:,})"


def card(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    """A model card in the spirit of TRIPOD+AI: intended use, data, outcome, inputs, performance
    (CV and, if confirmed, test), limitations — generated from the committed run records."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name} — run it first")
    cfg = r["config"]
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "none")
    md = f"""# Model card — `{name}` (round {round_id})

{cfg.get("description", "")}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intended use** | {"LEARNING ONLY — not for promotion (decisions.md O48)" if cfg.get("learning_only") else "Population-level planning aid for primary-care care management; not a diagnosis, not for emergencies"} |
| **Outcome** | `{cfg["label"]}` — {cfg.get("outcome_phrase", "see the round report")} (year 2 of a MEPS two-year panel) |
| **Population** | US civilian non-institutionalised adults (18+) in MEPS panels 21–27, observed in both years |
| **Training data** | Panels 21–25 (2016–2021); evaluation by leave-one-panel-out cross-validation |
| **Test data** | Panels 26–27 (2021–2023), scored once after a holdout-ledger entry |
| **Inputs** | {len(cats)} categorical + {len(nums)} numeric features (`{cfg["features"]}`); text representations: {text} |
| **Model** | `{cfg["model"]}`, task `{cfg["task"]}`, params {"round-001 tuned" if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or "defaults")} |
| **Cross-validated performance** | {_fmt_metrics(r["cv"])} |
| **Cross-validated baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(r.get("cv_baseline"))} |
| **Test performance** | {_fmt_metrics(c["test"]) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Test baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(c.get("test_baseline")) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Data provenance** | manifest sha256 `{r["provenance"]["manifest_sha256"][:12]}…`, code `{(r["provenance"]["git_commit"] or "unknown")[:12]}` |

## Limitations

- Trained on MEPS **self-reported** survey data; customer records differ (codes, charges vs payments,
  missing income). Recalibrate and validate on customer data before any use (Phase 8b).
- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.
- Explanations describe what the model weighed, not causes.
- **Uplift / impactability is not assessable with MEPS** (no intervention data — O37): this model ranks
  risk, not who would benefit from outreach.
- Subgroup fairness by race/ethnicity and insurance is not yet reported on this card.
"""
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md)
    return out


HUMAN_CRITERIA = {
    "measurable_in_customer_data": "Can a customer's own FHIR / claims data observe this outcome (needed to validate and recalibrate)?",
    "actionable": "What would a care manager do differently for a flagged patient?",
    "lead_time": "Is there time to act before the outcome happens?",
    "fhir_representability": "Probability -> RiskAssessment natively; count / cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35).",
    "regulatory_posture": "Does this change the FDA clinical-decision-support position?",
}


def scorecard(round_id: str, name: str, criteria: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """The target scorecard (O36): ML criteria filled from the records; non-ML criteria from a
    person's JSON ({criterion: {"score": ..., "rationale": ...}}) — or marked as still owed."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name}")
    human = json.loads(Path(criteria).read_text()) if criteria else {}
    cv, base = r["cv"], r.get("cv_baseline")
    m = c["test"] if c else cv
    lines = [f"# Target scorecard — `{r['config']['label']}` via `{name}` (round {round_id})", "",
             "| Criterion | Source | Assessment |", "|---|---|---|"]
    if "auroc" in m:
        lines += [f"| Discrimination | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f}, AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f}"
                  + (f" (baseline AUROC {base['auroc']:.3f}, CV)" if base else "") + " |",
                  f"| Calibration | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Brier {m['brier']:.4f}; mean predicted {m['mean_pred']:.3f} vs rate {m['rate']:.3f} |",
                  f"| Base rate | data | {m['rate']:.1%} |",
                  f"| Worklist value | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | top 10%: {m['top10_ppv']:.0%} have the outcome; they hold {m['top10_sensitivity']:.0%} of all cases |",
                  f"| Adults 65+ | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m.get('auroc_65plus', float('nan')):.3f} |"]
    else:
        lines += [f"| Ranking | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Spearman {m['spearman']:.3f} |"]
    for key, question in HUMAN_CRITERIA.items():
        entry = human.get(key)
        cell = (f"**{entry['score']}** — {entry['rationale']}" if entry
                else f"_TO BE SCORED BY A PERSON_ — {question}")
        lines.append(f"| {key.replace('_', ' ').capitalize()} | person | {cell} |")
    lines.append("| Uplift / impactability | — | Not assessable with MEPS (no intervention data — O37) |")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        lines += ["", "**Learning-only target (O48): not eligible for promotion.**"]
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "scorecards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return out


def promote(round_id: str, name: str, decision: str) -> Path:
    """Write the promotion record (O33) — only for a confirmed, carded, non-learning-only run whose
    promotion is backed by an existing decisions.md entry."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"O\d+", decision):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"decision must look like O49, got {decision!r}")
    if f"| {decision} |" not in DECISIONS.read_text():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{decision} is not in {DECISIONS} — record the decision first")
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if c is None:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no test-panel confirmation")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} is a learning-only target (O48)")
    card_path = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    if not card_path.exists():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no model card — run `card` first")
    model = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    if hashlib.sha256(model.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != c["fitted_model_sha256"]:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{model} does not match the model that was confirmed")
    record = {"round": round_id, "run": name, "decision": decision, "label": r["config"]["label"],
              "model_sha256": c["fitted_model_sha256"],
              "model_card_sha256": hashlib.sha256(card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    out = model.with_suffix(".PROMOTION.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return out

        rows.append(g.reset_index().assign(year=year))

    no_signal = (Xte.getnnz(axis=1) == 0)                   # nothing in common with any training name
    return {"class_accuracy": float((matched.cls.to_numpy() == test.cls.to_numpy()).mean()),
